With Ruxpin finally recovered, the team briefs him on the previous run. Echo splits off for some downtime- a celebrity chef has a rare pop-up event that they want to attend. They start trying to figure out how to access the ANIMUS facility hidden under Washington Bridge for Vida Nova. First, they follow up on a tip, and hire a Ratboy to lead them around the area in the Underground. With a significant time investment and some good luck, they eventually find a fully sealed passage leading a few blocks from the encased bridge facility to what looks like a parking structure. Using her navigation skills, Otters figures out that it is hidden under a former USPS parking garage in North Harlem.

They leave Ruxpin and Bug belowground, given that Ruxpin is kitted out in heavy armor and power glove, and Bug is Bug, and go to surveil the garage. Breeze pays Kobold to get him a ticket there, which he leans over a barricade to grab, and then uses to gain entry through the security door. Aradia and Breeze act a big show of “dude where’s my car” for the cameras, while they poke around, with Aradia assensing and Otters scanning through vision modes herself and via drone.

They find a few cars that look to have been there a while in the lower level, and are able to tell there is a warded space behind the wall, concealed by some sort of complex multi-part mechanism. Otters hides some drones onsite and has them check in a random schedule. They head back to the Underground entrance, in the basement of a soul food spot, and all get some food, bringing some down for Ruxpin and Bug as well. After a few hours waiting, Otters gets a hit from the drones- a van, looking like it could be Gramius or another similar ANIMUS driver, pulls in.

One of the cameras in the basement flashes some kind of code to the van, and then the two parked cars the team had noticed both rotate out on some kind of turntable system, leaving just enough room for the van to drive between them through the wall that opened up behind them. It descends a steep ramp, and presumably goes down into the concealed parking area they found in the Underground as the door closes behind it and the cars rotate back to their position.

The team debates means of approach- they could try to intercept the van, but based on what they know about the vans, and Gramius, they assume it will be hard to ID unless they hit it at the garage, which has heavy surveillance, and the driver will likely be a hard target as well. They discuss cutting or alchemically spell-shaping their way into the passageway Underground, since there are no entrances down there that they could find, but aren’t sure what they would find, what security measures might be alerted, and if Aradia could get them all in through the high force Ward.

Given all of that, they decide to focus on intercepting a courier and posing as them to gain entry, as Vida Nova had originally suggested. Since Aradia already got a good read on Stuart, and the team did a decent amount of surveillance on him without getting spotted (barely), and since he seems high level enough to be a worthwhile target, they decide to focus on him. They make a plan, get all the gear and prep they need to do done, and call up Mx. Seven to make sure the Null are ready to roll when needed. With that, Breeze heads down to Coney Island, to wait in the area Vida Nova had pointed out and try to spot Stuart headed up north.

Using a fake “down on his luck” SIN, he finds some other rougher looking types and joins their milling group while faking a phone call to an ex about whose fault everything was, to make sure noone wants to approach him. He eventually spots Stuart striding confidently towards his speed boat, doing good counter-surveillance as usual, but not nearly spotting Breeze this time. He calls it into the team and they get in position. Otters parks the sub low in the East River nearby, and then launches Bug (with an air tank) in one of the VTOLS, positioning him under the bridge, where he crawls around the sub-structure to find a good sniping post.

Otters then swings the VTOL back to pick herself up (also with air tank) while using the other VTOL to drop Ruxpin down into the river near the dock that Stuart uses. He stands on the bottom with Otters’ water jet, waiting. Aradia, on the shore, conjures up a water spirit and gets it in position, along with a multi-sensory illusion. As Stuart’s speedboat approaches, Aradia has the water spirit crash a wave into it, slowing it and throwing Stuart off-balance, as she also drops the illusion of a normal Stuart in speedboat over the scene.

Prepared, Bug gets off two quick shots with his rifle, the Stick’N’Shock rounds proving extra effective on the soaked Stuart, who tumbles from the back of the boat, where Otters has used the water jet to position Ruxpin. Ruxpin hooks up the medkit to Stuart, dosing him with Slab, and limiting the oxygen he will require Ruxpin to share to keep him alive. Ruxpin, spotting the secure courier wristband clasped around his wrist, rips off the hand and wristband and tosses them up to Aradia, on the bank.

Aradia, meanwhile, skims the surface of Stuart’s mind, using Ruxpin as the lynchpin for the spell. Even KO’ed and drugged, he has impressive mental defenses. She gets the code and entry protocol to the facility, and knows that he was meant to deliver his message of the day directly to one of the staff doctors, but not much else. Good enough! Aradia grabs the hand and bracelet, and tries to shove her hand through, only partially succeeding. Using the final service from the water spirit, she has it bring the speedboat to the dock, maintaining her illusion until it arrives, and the stepping off in her Stuart disguise- matching his aura with metamagic, and matching his look (inclluding proper wristband position) with another illusion.

She heads over to the access panel Bug found hidden behind the bench, as Breeze calls into Mx. Seven, who say they will deal with the anthrodrones, and await the team getting an open channel to the facility interior. Bug spots the jogger drones all take up a different security perimeter as they seem to fall under Null control. Aradia uses Stuart’s hand to activate the touchpad, and then uses his fingers to enter the alphanumeric code. The stair open behinds her, and she descends, tossing the loose hand off into the shadows of the bridge.

She does her best Stuart impersonation to the guards and receptionist she finds there, and manages to stand her ground, not giving over her courier delivery, which seems to require a thumbprint that isn’t Stuart’s to open. She is ushered into a patient room and told to wait til the doctor that the delivery for is available. Meanwhile, Otters has positioned herself right by the irising trash chute in the other VTOL, and uses her custom made wedge and spreader tool to jam into and crank it open. Some alerts flash on some system lights but with how offline this whole place is, the team hopes it will take the facility a bit to notice and get someone out to check on it.

Otters starts a snake drone up the waste-slicked, steep chute, hauling a data cable with it. She finds a compactor, with another sealed hatch above it, this one looks like a standard industrial trash chute door. She carefully navigates the snake through the compactor, slipping the data cable into nooks and crannies to ensure it isn’t crushed or severed. She reaches the next portal, and waits for someone to dump some trash. Inside, Aradia has rebuffed a nurse also offering to take delivery for the busy doctor, and finally gets taken back to see her. She used her time in the patient room to get one data tap in place on a locked terminal, for once the Null get access.

She heads back, and gets a cursory greeting from the doc, who uses her thumb to unlock the courier wristband, which Aradia has to carefully position to line up her illusion with the doctor’s touch. She grabs a data chip from inside, and Aradia (as Stuart still) is told to leave. The nurse who’s been escorting her seems to know and dislike Stuart. Aradia does her best to stall, insisting on using the bathroom but finding no terminals there, and then using an illusion of Stuart tying his shoes while she goes invisible and silent, to sneak back to the doctor’s room and get a data tap on her computer to try to see what was on that chip she delivered.

Unfortunately, Aradia isn’t very good at sleight of hand tricks and the doctor sees the data tap right away. The doctor yanks it out and calls security before Aradia can drop her with a massive Agony spell and plug it back in. Luckily, a custodian (who is also another armed guard) dumps the trash at that moment, allowing Otters to sneak the drone in and gets comms up to Aradia and the Null. Mx. Seven announces that they are starting the hack, and Aradia decides to beat feet, heading for the trash chute as her spells and illusions start to get detected.

One of the guards emerges wearing a large contraption on his head that seems to allow him to see through her illusions, and takes a shot at her which she only avoids by the smallest degree, and feels she has permanently used up some of her luck in doing so. She dives out the trash chute, with the Null seemingly opening it for her and preventing the guards on her tail from opening it again or starting the compactor as she slithers through and slides down, dropping into the river, where Ruxpin catches her and gives her some oxygen while she summons an air spirit to envelop her.

Mx. Seven reports that the systems are heavy duty but old, so they are getting good results. Otters starts exfil, as Breeze gets off the train he was taking up to them to get some Indian food, since the job is done, with Echo stopping by to join him. Otters scoops up Aradia first, and noticing that she doesn’t have any air supplies, just flies her back to the safehouse instead of trying to get her in the sub. She brings herself with air tank to the sub, and hangs on the outside for now. She next picks up Bug from under the bridge, and drops him with air tank off at the sub before swinging back to grab Ruxpin.

Ruxpin, taking the initiative, drowns Stuart and shoves his body into the trash chute, laying his arm across the open portal and then yanking Otters’ wedge tool out, causing the portal to slice shut, and explaining the absent hand, the alert from the trash chute, etc, pinning the blame all on Stuart (hopefully). Based on what Aradia heard inside, Stuart has had a fall from grace in Indica Meiers eyes, given all the leaks and exposures ANIMUS has recently suffered, and he seemed quite proud, so a disgruntled recently demoted spy seems like a good motivation. Regardless, with Ruxpin now also retrieved, they open the sub hatch and take on some water while all loading in, shoving it closed and venting the water as Otters takes them back down to the sub.

They check in with Mx. Seven, who reports that they’ve been cut off from the systems again (the data cable being cut when Ruxpin closed the irising hatch) but got some good intel. As much of it was heavily encrypted and encoded it will take some time to process, to they will report back. For now, they have more patient data, much like what they found at The Octagon. With Brinkvale having helped them comprehend the other batch, they can make better sense of this bunch, and once again recognize some people they know amongst the anonymous patient ID’s.

They pass this along to VN with the promise of more, leaving out the Null’s involvement. She seems thrilled with their work, and pays them a job fee for now, with more coming depending on info quality. With that out of the way, the team rests up a bit, while Aradia ponders her future in the shadows- it’s been a lot of close ones lately, and she’s debating taking on a more backseat role to assist in her continued longevity. However, the team is on the hook for a job of the Null next, in exchange for the Null’s help on this one, so they start readying to tackle that.

Hype also makes good on his threats, and they all take a hit to their rep, though their proactive management blunts the worst of it and they are mostly able to shunt it aside with ease.

The team heals for a few days aboard the CTRL Salt Delete, and Otters has a flashback, thinking that she actually had seen The Octagon, or somewhere similar, before. Wanting control over her own memories, she gets Aradia to probe into the recesses of her mind. Aradia overdoes it a little bit reducing Otters’ (minimal) willpower as prep, and Otters slips into a light coma. Aradia also uses her new MindNet spell to link up with the other teammates and telepathically share what she discovers. Ruxpin, the most badly injured, continues recovering in a Valkyrie module.

They sift through some of Otters’ memories, and find that she may have been on CIA (or UCAS black ops in general) payrolls as some sort of contractor, in addition to her kidnapping TM’s for MCT. They recognize a few places and figures in her mind- the MCT shadow liaison in NYC, Evan Teeg, hands Otters over to Indica Meiers of the CIA, at a facility that certainly looks to be the Octagon. Otters also seems to recognize someone else in her subconscious as the memory emerges, and Aradia chases, getting the name and image of a very bland human, Stuart, who seems to run the day to day at the facility, while Meiers is more high level perhaps.

The team asks some questions and probes around more, but doesn’t find anything else of use. When Otters wakes up as Aradia stops suppressing her Will, she is excited to bond with Echo about both being government agents, of a sort, though Echo is mildly non-plussed (but handles it well). With that, they rest another day for Aradia to recover from a bunch of heavy casting, and then realize they better get after this paydaya if they want to get anything for it, since The Tiding also ended up with a copy, though possibly lacking some of the context.

They head over to Brinkvale’s, who says he is happy to review the data but will need a bit, and asks them to go peacefully convince Sigurd, the Valkyrie they encountered in Central Park, to return for more therapy and scans after she ran off. They eventually track her down to a local restaurant/brewpub that passes her some extra food from time to time, and bug surveils the side entrance until she arrives. Echo comes out, partially to stop Breeze from taking the lead, and smoothly gets Sigurd to remember them.

Echo figures out that she seems to be humming something, and recognizes some kind of Euro classical. She says she needs to dance and hear other music to get it out of her head, as it it bothering her, and Echo agrees to take her out clubbing tonight, rattling off a few options of the hot spots in town that Heat was invested in. They head over to Central Park, with Otters, Aradia, and Breeze hanging back and getting some street food, while Echo talks up the doorman at Club Interrobang to get Bug and Sigurd in, as appropriately alt people.

Bug actually has a really nice time, and is given an interesting custom drink by the Free Spirit bartender- perfectly divided down the middle when served with some sort of gel, the drink inter-mingles over time, perhaps representing Bug’s two personas. Sigurd also has fun, tossing back a long series of flaming shots on Bug’s tab. Abyssa is there, and plays a Heat track, but sped up even further, which is announced as “AN ABYSSAL REMIIIIIIIX” by the DJ. The crowd seems confused by the 5 second blast of noise, but Bug manages to do a cool standing flip into a death drop, impressing the crowd and earning a small raised eyebrow from Abyssa.

They leave shortly after, as Sigurd is trashed and gets cut off. She starts half stumbling and half flying off into the Park, where the team catches up with her and gets her to agree to go along to Brinkvale’s for some scans, with her and Brinkvale both in part explaining that the last treatment seems to have been an effort to replace some of her missing memories with a nice BTL of a night at the opera, but that her brain seems to have recognized the falsehood and rejected. Breeze impresses her with his frequency of dying, but she says he has a way to go as a warrior as he keep getting sent back and not accepted into Valhalla.

He gets into some philosophy in response, which seems earnest but cringey. They walk her back to the maglev to Brinkvale’s, and get the scans done easily on arrival. She takes off quickly but agrees to return for more, non-BTL, care in the future. Brinkvale explains that they are seeing the memory alterations and blocks break down quicker in the Central Park batch of patients, since they were seemingly released mid-treatment. Putting together some bits and pieces of intel, the team determines there is likely some sort of internal power struggle happening at ANIMUS, as Jonathan Blake runs the security there, and seems to be likely to be the person behind the release of patients, as well as to tipping Piper Jinx off to them.

Both Blake and Meiers interviewed the team, using Piper as an intermediary again, so it seems like those two could represent two opposing factions within the program, or the two could be aligned against an as yet unknown third party. Regardless, interesting, and possibly useful. Brinkvale breaks down the patient data and relays to the team that it shows that even it patients whose treatment was completed, ANIMUS is having a lot of problems with both replication and stability, especially in the longterm. There’s also just a ton of patient data, which he is excited to continue sifting through.

They agree to keep working with him on this, after doing some careful social checks to make sure he’s still on the level, and he scans Otters’ brain as well. He points out how the older alteration was done more crudely than the current technique, but is still exhibiting some of the same failure points, and is excited to hear about the return of some of Otters’ memories. The team heads off, receiving a call from Hype which Breeze naively answers. Aradia takes over and brushes off his threats and insinuations, sticking to the line that the team wants a clean break from Horizon after Heat’s exit.

Since they’ve already done some proactive rep management and also have a lot of new members, they aren’t too worried right now, so Aradia also politely rejects Hype’s offer to get square with Horizon in return for all their ANIMUS data, in addition to a hefty payday. Breeze seems to like Hype and is surprised by the group response, but is happy to go along with it. He also starts learning how to take people’s guns, as that seems like a flaw in his current approach, based on the last mission. They next follow up on Brinkvale’s suggestion to seek out the E-ghost of his old mentor at NYU, from before he went rogue.

With some tips from him and a decent payout to Kobold, they gain access to a hidden research host, tucked inside the NYU medical school matrix host. There, they find the E-ghost of Dr. Sonya Peters along with some copies of herself and a few other digital colleagues, who seem to also have continued their work after death. She initially rebuffs them until Aradia and Echo team up to catch her interest with a quick synopsis of what they are working on. She gives them a little time before turning back to her work- she seems quite haughty and not sad to no longer need sleep- and informs them that a man she assumes was a CIA or similar spook (who matches Stuart’s description) approached her around a year back, shortly before her death.

He attempted to recruit her into something that sounds a lot like ANIMUS as the team describes it to her, and seemed disappointed by her rejection. She believed, based on the limited info she was presented, that there was no way they could be developing and using the tech ethically based in their timeline and prospectus, and was also sketched out that they wouldn’t reveal the ID of either party of funders in what was described to her as a public/private co-initiative. Shortly after her refusal, she developed an aggressive cancer out of nowhere, which quickly killed her. She says that luckily she had taken precautions to prevent the loss to the world of her brilliant mind, but that she wouldn’t disapprove if the team took a little righteous revenge for her unnecessarily early departure from the corporeal realm. She pass along a comm number that Stuart had given her to to call if she changed her mind, which she never used.

The team decides to sell this latest data to Vida Nova, making clear that it isn’t fully exclusive, re: the Tiding having a copy, and then plan to also pass a copy to Old Soup a bit after VN, to stay on his good side as well.
Echo also finally hears from Adelaide White, the ex-CIA vamp scientist who is a long way from her own time, and puts her in touch with VN, who seems delighted by the oddness and depravity of what is effectively a cannibalistic time traveller. The team also assembles a composite image of Stuart from their minds, and runs it through MonaLisa, getting a result that confirms their suspicions. Instead of a “no match” or similar, it looks to Echo like someone has been making an ongoing effort to scrub images of Stuart from searchable databases, implying he is still active and connected.

VN offers to pick them up, and grabs them off the street in her combo box truck/office. Following up on Breeze’s request, she has her fighting torso on, and dislocates his shoulder with some aggressive arm wrestling, perhaps proving her point. She helps him get it back into joint, and then continues with the meeting. She agrees to the terms, buys the data, and seems happy they came to her first. She says she’ll look into it all and get back to them soon with some likely follow up work. The next day she calls with a lead- she managed to track the commlink, which seemed to primarily be in two areas, one zone around Coney Island, and one around Washington Height/North Harlem.

The team decides to surveil the Harlem/Washington Heights end, and Echo eventually lucks out and spots Stuart mooring a small cigarette boat and hopping ashore. The team starts tailing, with Breeze and Echo on foot and Morticia in the air, while Aradia makes an approach in the astral. Bug hangs back for support with Otters in the van. The boat also explains the odd signal VN got from the comms- he was bouncing between relay towers while speed-boating up the river, likely commuting between this site, The Octagon, and whatever is in Coney Island (maybe just the boat storage and convenient ferry access). Aradia gets a good look at his essence- he’s non-magical, but has a lot of well-concealed high-end implants. She then breaks off when he checks a leech band on his wrist, seemingly warned of her astral presence nearby.

Echo has to split off next, as Stuart seems quite skilled, and almost spots them while checking for tails. Breeze is next to fall back, when Stuart makes a series of 4 right turns to check for tails again. He doesn’t confront any of them, so they aren’t sure if they were made or if he is just thorough. Either way, he’s good. Luckily, Otters is able to keep Moritica on target, and maybe due to the various close calls on the ground, Stuart isn’t looking up much, so she sees him duck under one of the spars of the Washington Bridge to the Bronx, step behind a pedestrian bench, and then disappear. There’s a jogging path down by the river, but no good way to get Morticia down that low without exposing her, so Bug heads in as he hasn’t been seen yet.

He pokes around the area a bit, and is glad Morticia saw something, as he otherwise never would have found it. Tucked behind the bench, up against the bridge and concealed between two supports, is a panel in the ground. The seam is barely visible as it was just used, and would likely be quickly covered by dirt and debris after an normal passage of time. Aradia does a flyby and can’t see through, but spots traces of a high-power, well-concealed ward inside. Bug finds one section of the panel that isn’t covered in turf and is actually a hologram of grass and dirt, that seems to lead to some sort of access controls, but as he can’t see them and doesn’t want to trip any alarms he backs off for now.

While the rest of the team has been watching this, they also spot a set of suspicious joggers on a patrol around the area, all of which seem to be VERY high-end anthroform drones, when examined closer. They blend in well though. They don’t notice other overt security, but this already seems like a tough one. Otters calls up Eduard Cabrera of the Rat Pack, and talks architecture and Underground with him. Comparing notes, they can see that when the bridge was rebuilt post-quakes, the Manhattan end was built a lot larger, in terms of supports, casings, pilings, and other sub-structure, than the Bronx end, and there is no access to the large footprint in the Underground, so no knowing what someone might have tucked away in there.

Otters takes some drones out on a recon mission, first bringing herself under the bridge in one of the new VTOL’s, and taking a look around. She spots what looks like a trash port, that irises open from the inside, and decides to risk using mana drops to get more intel. Unfortunately, she has a hard time interpreting the data and gets a little freaked out, so sends Aradia down again to try as well. She gets a better read, and has a feeling this is how the facility dumps waste of all kinds, including failed test subjects, so it has a bad vibe in the astral. But could certainly be one way in. Thinking about it, they decide this is unlikely to just be a safehouse and must be another full ANIMUS facility, as they had seen some fragmented memories in patient’s minds of both an island location (the Octagon) and somewhere in the city (here?).

They report in to VN again, and she congratulates them on the successful recon, saying she will observe for a bit and get back to them. While debating how to get in, as they assume they will need to, they decide that perhaps they should follow up with Cat on her reluctant collaboration with the Null Sect, as if they do a job for the Null, maybe the Null could help them with this job. Cat sets a meeting, again as Castle Clinton in Battery City. The team heads over and spots SPYder doing some surveillance as they approach, he gives them a friendly nod. They find Cat waiting in some chav-y casual wear, alongside a very bland looking salaryman type, who seems a little awkward.

They introduce themselves as Mx. Seven, or “Explorer Primary 7” for their full title. They explain that they are quite comfortable in “outer worlds” and excited to explore further, though they hold themselves a bit oddly and talk to loud, seeming to have some trouble with volume modulation. Regardless, they have a job for the team and are happy to trade assistance on the team’s job for the team’s assistance on theirs. As a gesture of good faith, they agree to tackle the team’s job first, and say that the anthrodrones will be no issue, and that further hacking assistance should be simple so long as the team brings along some data taps and transmitters.

They also hand over a backup of similar gear, along with some mapping drones, for the team to use on their job when they get to it- infiltrating, mapping and data tapping a nearby AZT warehouse complex, which Mx. 7 believes contains some hidden levels, as well as some useful intel in their search for a pathway to Dis, reiterating once again that the Null are, of course, natural explorers. The team makes the deal, with various degrees of uneasiness, and reports back to VN, leaving the specifics out. She tells them that her best idea after observing the site is to intercept Stuart or one of the couriers that occasionally visit, get a copy of whatever message they are carrying, and then pose as them to deliver it, or pose as Stuart if they are up for it. Courier seems easier, so that’s the plan for the time being.

In bed with the Null! Should at least prove to be effective.

Octagon in 60 Seconds
5/26/2025, 12:15:19 PM
Runners
Otters aka Roadkill
Aradia
Ruxpin
Bug
Breeze

The team spends a while discussing a train trip to visit Boston, after Breeze reads a bunch in the team files and gets fascinated by Mama and some of the other strange biz going on up there. Since noone on the team currently has a personal connection, this doesn’t feel very high priority, though some on the the team are interested to hear how involved PepperJack was in much of it. For now, they decide to focus on the job they have, to investigate the mysterious Octagon, having finally located it on Roosevelt Island, amidst the maxsec prisons. Given the high security, the approach looks difficult, so they do some recon. Attracted to the thought of some R’N’R, Echo takes this one off to go on a day trip to a Korean spa nearby.

The Octagon has been built into a larger complex, with large additional wings to the west and south added on. There is a semi-detached 4th floor on the west building which connects to the Octagon’s cupola, which seems to have been all closed in, with no exterior doors or windows. Morticia spots a pair of guards in the lobby entrances to the west and south buildings, with no exterior entrances left on the Octagon itself, which seems to serve as a connective passage between the two, though it’s lower 3 floors still have windows at least. The guards seem to be better equipped and trained then expected, though wearing generic SECURITY uniforms.

There is no land passage available to the island, with ferry and aerial tram being the public options, and few roads on the island, with most of it being fenced off prison property or what looks to be a mined ring around the exterior, aside from the 2 ferry landings, one on the Manhattan side and one on the Queens side. There are 2 bridges from Manhattan that go over the island but neither touch down, though the northern Queensborough Bridge is close to crossing over the Octagon and not overly high off the ground. Ruxpin calls Magnus Jam while Otters contacts Eduard Cabrera from the Rat Pack to get the lowdown on the “collapsed” F train line that runs under the island.

Both give variations on the same details- the tunnel is traversible, but the station for the island has aggressive auto-turrets with a “shoot first” policy. Theoretically it could be a path in, since it is more focused on keeping people on the island and preventing escapes, but it would still be dicey. Also, that station is the meeting place where Tamanous picks up their purchases from among the prisoners, usually the SINless and others the prison wardens and guards are happy to “lose track of” for a healthy bribe. So, while this is an option, it doesn’t seem overly promising.

Aradia does an astral flyby, and spots 3 spirits, one patrolling each wing and one just watching the enclosed 4th floor and cupola on the Octagon. She traces them back to a powerful mage posted up in the south building, though she has to retreat before he spots her before she can get a good enough look to imitate his signature. She does determine that the cupola area is warded, that the south building is likely dedicated to patient care, that the west building seems like an admin center, and that the background count should remain around 2, with an aura of despair, as long as she steers clear of specific worse spots in the patient wing.

Given the lack of signage or any other clear markers, it looks like this is some kind of private medical facility. As opposed to the 5 large prisons on the island, it is not itself fenced, though the parking lot off of Main Street has a gate arm. It seems they are relying on anonymity and the security of the island itself. Still without a workable plan, Aradia talks the team into trading the 4 Oyabun/MCT internal financial shenanigans data to The Tiding in exchange for some further intel, and Breeze puts Kobold on retainer for the duration of the job, stocking up on some data taps to get her access when needed.

The Tiding comes through- they report that the site uses suppliers affiliated with the UCAS government, supporting a CIA connections. However, Breeze’s plan to intercept a shipment is complicated by the fact that the security contractor, Centurion, manages all the transport logistics as well as securing the site itself. This is also interesting in that the team knows that Centurion is wholly owned by Jonathan Blake, the mayor of Bellevue in Seattle, who recently paid them to lie to Buttercup and the Nagato Combine about AA’s death and their involvement. Also, that Silver Nail had surveilled Blake and Indica Meiers, the local CIA high level operative, meeting at the known Black Lodge-owned Belvedere Castle in Central Park. So something is up there.

The Tiding also report that the Cupola area and attached hall to the west building 4th floor are Faraday’ed, and that there is a 4-person strong guard post at the west building end, which is the only access. So it seems like the cupola is their target for seeking hidden intel, but how to get in…. After some debate, Breeze suggests taking a page from some of his old Bollywood trids, and jumping down off the nearby bridge on a cable, busting through a wall, and dragging the computer out with a souped up car. Halo Hunting

While the rest of the team is vamp hunting and exploring new areas of the Underground, Ruxpin is following up on leads around town for his missing teammate Halo. Amidst shopping for the next Underground investigation for Old Soup, the team decides to accompany Echo to another Top Secret debrief with Col. Mattison at Black Arrow Brigade HQ. In this confidential setting she explains further, though. It seems that Heat, after leaving the team, made good on his parting intent of linking up with Prot0 and other “extremist” TM’s to seek revenge against the corps who kidnap and experiment on them. He brought along the intel he had about Colloton’s final task, infiltrating The Towers (the Corp Court’s earthside HQ) to get intel from and do a frame job on Diasruiz, who Colloton believes to be the primary corporate architect of the Blackouts. Her survival: optional. Heat seems to have called in all his SkyBrides shares, and with the help of Prot0’s band of TM’s, in their new alliance with the GOD-Slayers, gained access to her private quarters, used her biometrics to access her devices either before or shortly after killing her, ripped a bunch of stored data off her devices, and then set a copy of the Discidium virus lose on the Corp Court servers from her terminals once they were being forced out, through their Foundation access.

Colloton explains that this outbreak will almost surely be siloed to The Towers host, but that it will likely sow some righteous chaos there in the meantime, even if it doesn’t spread to other corp servers. She also says that if anyone needs to allay any ill feelings about Diasruiz’ death, some of the evidence they found show that she was one of SK’s internal Monad/Crackhaus hunters during the early CFD crisis, rising to the rank of Grand Inquisitor before being rewarded with the appointment to the Court. Colloton also shares some of the other recovered intel, which she says they will be releasing through trusted media over the next while; Diasruiz was indeed the Court’s leader in corralling votes and support for the secret Blackout plan, though ARES were of course also enthusiastic participants.

However, it quickly got out of hand- it seems that the Court wanted a simple on/off switch with which they could easily target grids, matrix, etc, but would be able to reactivate it. They quickly switched to spin and PR control, keeping their own involvement hidden among rumors of dragons, Horrors, Null (true, but still), Ordo Maximus, Black Lodge and others being behind it. Though many of these groups benefited in the short term at least, the Court seems to have been the primary actor, and DelaMar’s deal with the Null seems to have been a component of the deal to gain their aid. Colloton says she won’t be regularly contactable for some time, but encourages Echo to keep working with Mattison as needed.

Otters pulls up the panelling and Breeze and Bug muscle it out of the way while Otters carefully plants det cord to blow the floor down into the cavity below. They find the bodies of some commuters, long decayed and predated, trapped under some rubble from the long ago earthquakes where part of the station collapsed, but there seem to be less bodies that there should be, based on the tunnel collapses on both sides and no other obvious ways in/out.

They radar scan the filthy, near stagnant river where the tracks used to be, and find the other bodies, though are also surprised to be attacked by a Basilisk, which attempts to petrify Echo, before Aradia distracts it with an illusion, and Otters, Breeze, Echo, and Bug all team up to finish it off. They notice that it is fairly emaciated, and see that there are only small spaces in the tunnels where rats and small scavengers could have crawled in, so it seems after feasting and growing to size on the initial trapped victims, it has likely gotten too big to itself leave, and been subsisting on whatever makes it’s way in. The good news, as Otters reports, is that they are unlikely to encounter other critters down here- anything bigger would have eaten the Basilisk, and it would have eaten anything smaller.

They explore a bit, eventually levitating across the river to explore a rusted shut maintenance door. They head to it, and Otters and Breeze team up on the ancient keypad lock to get it powered back up and then bypass it, with Breeze again muscling the wheeled handle to break the rust coating and get it turning. They haul the massive door open, surprised when it moves smoothly, and feel air rush in past them as the pressure equalizes- it seems like the space behind was airtight for some time, and smells stale and vaguely medical.

They hear a distant generator sputter and kick on, with a few hazy emergency lights coming on as well. They seem to be in some sort of lab facility, so it looks like they found the right place at least. They head forward, through another smaller, open hatch, and find a hallway with a door ahead and doors to either side. They check ahead first, going through another hatch to find an elevator platform, but are relived that this is the bottom of the elevator shaft, and the shaft itself is filled with rubble, so this is effectively the only level of this facility they can explore. Checking the door on either side of the hall to the elevator, they find two labs, each with 4 cots, and 4 chairs with restraints, and various IV’s and medical devices. Checking over stuff, Otters finds that they seem to have been injecting their “patients” with psychoactive substances, and extreme doses of other drugs and compounds.

Echo finds a side door into the elevators that leads to a narrow one-way observation room, looking into the labs, They surmise that they are in 1/4 of a circular lab, with an outer ring hall running around the wedges, and a smaller circle in the middle comprised of elevator platforms facing each lab area and the observation rooms. They continue, finding a dormitory, seemingly for staff, based on the presence of old desktop terminals and mussed bedding. No useful evidence otherwise emerges, though they strap the terminals to the Mule drone to bring along. Heading further in, they find the 2nd lab wedge, similar layout to the first, but this time they seem to have been experimenting with sound and visuals on their “patients”. They are disturbed when they hear another distant, though closer now, sound as the generator suddenly shuts off and the lights go out.

Navigating by flashlight again, they continue, finding a storage room, where the remains of air and water filtration systems (long overtaxed) and empty MRE containers are all that remain, aside from the generator, which seems to have plenty of fuel, but when they check, has been quickly sabotaged. Hearing a distant thud, Breeze, Otters and Aradia race back to the entrance, not wanting to get trapped, while Echo and Bug stay behind to try to get the generator back up. This proves relatively simple, though they don’t waste time getting additional systems on, just some lights again for now. Meanwhile, the other team finds the door shut, and then is ambushed by two emaciated vamps, once in a lab coat and one in a tattered security uniform.

Breeze and Aradia, using her weapon focus, manage to take out the security vamp before the lab coated one asks to make a deal, explaining that they just woke and are desperately hungry. Echo and Bug amble up to join the negotiation, though the vamp seems a little haughty, and responds poorly when Breeze tries to intimidate her, unleashing a Terrorscape that overwhelms most of the team mentally, sending them into a near catatonic state of terrified panic. Luckily, Bug and Echo hold it together, and the vamp, who introduces herself as Dr. Adelaide White, seems impressed by Echo’s resistance, as if she wants to study them. However, she’s cogent enough to make a deal, and agrees to pass over her personal devices and tell the team the rough outline of what happened here. She seems horrified to find out what year it is, having been down here nearly 70 years and dormant for most of that time, and also then horrifies Echo when they try to exchange contact info and all she has is a long dead palm pilot.

Echo givers her a credstick with some funds and writes down their comm number on some paper, before the doctor takes off, saying she will leave with her other colleague who shut the vault door and was waiting outside. As she exits, the Terrorscape finally fades and the rest of the team regains coherent thought. Some are a bit annoyed but agree the deal was actually a good one. Also, Echo seems to have unlocked a new Adept of the Analytical Path ability, and is able to gain them touchlink access to all the devices in the facility, after pondering how Heat was able to do that for a while. Otters powers them up one at a time, using the drone, and Echo accesses them, with the team’s Agents finding the once state of the art encryption to be child’s play.

They get a bunch on info about more CIA mind control experiments, and find that this facility was in contact with the other one they just found- promising paracritters were sent here for live experimentation after being ID’ed and verified at the other facility. Then, after these folks were trapped (they used an elevator hidden in the long-since-demolished condos above for primary access, with the train tunnel door being a backup) and with the train tunnel also collapsed, they decided to use a rare, pre-Awakening Vampire to infect the few surviving staff, who the team encountered, then killed the Vamp so that she couldn’t control them, as they assumed she would be more skilled and capable with her powers.

They then used their new mind control abilities to keep the surviving “patients” alive as a feeding pool as long as they could, til then ran out and had to purposefully shut everything down and seal the facility, venting out some air to induce a state of dormancy that they knew Vamps possessed from their studies. So these were definitely some evil or at least amoral people. The team suddenly realizes that they just let loose two hungry, amoral Vamps next to a coffin motel, with a bunch of sleeping people trapped in the air in small pods, and become worried about what they might find aboveground. SPYder gets hooked into some terminals and starts hacking while the team pokes around. Oddly, each desk has a pair of terminals, one a standard modern wireless terminal connected to the building host (still running on the Foundation), while the other is air-gapped and fully hardwired. There is no way to connect the two without cracking them open and rewiring them (except perhaps for TM’s), which seems odd- some kind of data partition. The team starts to worry that this might be either designed to keep the Null Sect in, or out. Of what they don’t know.

They also find offices for the 3 executives, which seem suspiciously generic and impersonal, and a shared secretarial office, where Bug finds a hand-written journal stashed way back in a desk drawer. This suggests that MCT’s Denver cleanup has gone beyond erasing Matrix evidence of their personnel having been on-site, but to erasing or altering those personnel’s memories as well.

With Bug thinking about some stuff, he comes up with the idea that since all 3 exec offices seem so similar, and since the secretary reports their weird behavior all seeming like they got some version of the same treatment, they decide to just check one of the exec’s, and only look into another one or 2 if the first one shows up anything unexpected. They carefully sneak past cleaning crews after using Echo’s light pistol to hit emergency stairwell cameras with Looper rounds. Bug breaks into the room where the executive seems to be sleeping, and Otters investigates via snake drone.

Seeing that the guy has drunk himself into a stupor, Aradia enters, Silenced and Invisible, and uses her newest spell, Reduce Willpower, before Mind Probing him. He resists a bit, even unconscious, obviously having had some corp training, but is no match. However, Aradia finds a strange mind- some things she seeks he only has surface responses to, with no subconscious activations- relating to their work onsite, NYC experiences etc. Some other stuff, related to Denver, has no surface thoughts and ONLY subconscious stuff, though even that seems vague and distant. Aradia tries to surface some memories, and also examines what he remembers of his dreams- it does seem that, as with Otters, the erasure is not perfect, so little things surface, but nothing fully provable.

Aradia gets a call from Anka that Siedah Legrange at the Freedom Tunnel reported that some plain clothes spook types came looking for the team shortly after they passed through after raiding the possible CIA safehouse, but that everyone there knows better than to talk to government types.

It does suggest that the BL was not driven as fully out of DeeCee as people thought, during the shadow conflict there a few years back.

The BL connection could certainly explain the high-level magical protection that Meiers is rumored to have access to, not explained otherwise given her lack of known magical ability. The team chills for a bit until they get a sudden call from Cat- they are needed again ASAP! Cat was tracking a shipment from some MCT docks in the Lower Westside, which seems to have gotten attacked by Ancients, though NYPD INC interrupted the whole affair and seems to have impounded the vehicle, arrested the driver, and grabbed a few Ancients as well in the mix. Luckily, the NYPD precinct they all got brought to is the border station between North Terminal and the Lower West Side, so the team turns off their SINs, throws on some disguises, grabs all their heavy combat gear, and heads over to the crossing, finding a scene of some chaos. With Morticia overhead, the team gets a good tactical view, and sees that there are escapees fleeing the NYPD lockup, as well as folks from Terminal scaling the impound lot wall to break into cars there, grabbing anything useful and tossing it back over. Since the checkpoint has auto-turrets (that seem on the fritz but are still aiming around wildly) the team decides to follow people over the wall, and using ropes, ladders, and levitation, does so smoothly. Otters gets levitated over the wall as well to help IRL, not her favorite. Hopefully the BTL maker’s recording can tell them the rest of the story, they just have to get there before someone (or something!) else does….

Even given the skill of their supporting UCAS deckers, this seems improbable.

Echo starts brainstorming strategies with the team, franctically trying to put together a plan on how to spin this….

He seems to view the team as a potential tool to advancement, and though the team doesn’t feel they can trust him, exactly, they feel they can trust his avarice. He shows them the machine, which he claims is a full-on sci-fi teleporter.

The team is glad they didn’t storm the place, as it looks to take a team of 15 scientists to run and calibrate it all. Otters, Heat and Aradia all examine it and can’t quite tell if it is magitech posing as sci-fi or if this is something entirely new. Regardless, they agree to the deal- transport to Caelum and the item they seek, in exchange for other weapons they will acquire for Prime. The CEO doesn’t want to lose this deal, so pressures them into going immediately instead of resting, which they eventually do. They find themselves strapped into chairs inside a concrete sphere, with high-tech wires, tubes, circuits, lights and the like running all around.

Lasers start to play across them as they find themselves staring down an infinite light tunnel. Most of them manage alright, though Ruxpin is a bit overwhelmed. They snap forward in an instant, or maybe forever, and find themselves strapped into similar chair, but in a wholly different room, all made of perfectly smooth metal and shiny white plastic. A four-legged, four-armed figure is patiently waiting as they gather themselves, with Otters also noticing that her drones have transformed again to match the paradigm, now truly looking horrific as their odd ZeCorp forms seem to have been seamlessly wrapped in metal and plastic. That said, they seem to be running incredibly well. StepMAMA however seems to be having some trouble, letting out an agonized digital scream before rebooting.

The figure in the middle, after an appropriate time, introduces itself as Legatum, or Ambassador if they prefer, which Echo is delighted by until they realize they’ve lost their adept abilities, which bums them out. Aradia also tries to cast a spell and can’t even access mana, feeling like the drain hits but then doesn’t actually effect her. She also sees all her reagents, foci, etc are inert though intact. Also stressful. Legatum explains that in their perfectly logical world, they have eliminated magic by scraping their biosphere clean some time ago. When the team tries to inquire further, Legatum states that this is unfortunately from a time in history before their current advanced record keeping, so details are light.

They get the rest of the briefing- most denizens of the plane are genderless and use “it” pronouns, though a variety of others are also common. Violence has been edited out of their reality, which the team confirms, becoming more stressed as their weapons and attack “work” but do no damage, and the only pain they feel is the momentary learned response before their nerves catch up and report no actual damage. This further stresses them out, especially Ruxpin, who as a combat specialist feels a little useless. He also notes that he is unable to shift form, seemingly due to the absence of magic.

They ask a lot of hypotheticals, as Echo can’t quite conceptualize how a violence-free society could function. Heat is also distressed to find that he is unable to comprehend the local matrix, even though he can sort of detect it. Otters and the others can’t even see it, and Legatum explains it is an order of magnitude more advanced than their, so they shouldn’t try to interact with it. More bad news. Also, since the locals have all taken more perfect forms, there is no need for food, drink, or sleep. Legatum encourages them to remove their ShadowCloaks and join in, but they refuse, so Legatum tells them it’s good they brought supplies, and that they can rest wherever they like and everyone will move around or over them, as they can’t be harmed.

The team all hunkers down, with some of them crashing from drugs as well, which some of the locals seem to find quite repellent, and presumably illogical. They awaken and regroup, and Legatum finds them again to continue the tour, taking them around the pristine, sterile planes of sci-fi metal and plastic towers, temples and the like, explaining the plane is a place of knowledge and learning. As they try to steer the convo towards where to seek weapons, Legatum warns them that that is a taboo and not to speak of it. Otters asks after intel on mind alteration, and is directed off towards a library dedicated towards biologicals, while the rest head to the Temple of Knowledge, the largest structure at the dead center of the plane, where the Archive is apparently kept, hoping to find something there.

Otters gets some intel on mind tech, and heads back to rejoin the team. Meanwhile, the team has inquired after Null Sect, Tan Robes, and some other things, and found that the plane has little info in magical or EI threats, as they view themselves as safe from them, and also have only recently re-established outside contact with Zecorp, and thereby secondhand contact with the Material Plane. After their inquiries are rebuffed by a few more archivists, the head archivist, a horrifying mechanical centipede, comes and brings them to it’s office, introducing itself as Scriniarii. It seems fascinated by violence and unconcerned about sharing dangerous weapons knowledge with them, as they won’t be able to use it here anyway. It seems to view them as primitives, but be very interested in what they know.

They eventually agree to allow it to brainscan them, with assurances that the scans will be anonymized and not be publicly accessible for over a decade. Scriniarii says it is a nearly lossless process, but doesn’t specify to whom, and the team mostly emerges unscathed, though some of Ruxpin’s military training seems to have vanished. They do however get a copy of the Discidium as promised, as well as some trash programs, which Scriniarii derides as low-tech placeholders to tide Prime over, a mean joke which it seems to enjoy participating in. Heat is also able to get a little more info about the plane’s past.

Apparently, after some largescale die-off (the team is assuming the most recent Scourge/Horror attack), the less-advanced machine life here managed to make some kind of deal with another entity to get rid of the rest of the bio-life (which they viewed as violent liars), and start building their “perfectly logical utopia” that the team sees before them now. The team is all feeling pretty ready to leave this place, and hopefully get all their abilities back, so they say goodbye to this weird creep in the archive basement, and head out to seek Legatum and get sent back.

Deeper into the Mountain

It actually is pretty good for their purposes: one small tunnel exit high on the mountainside, other paths closed off with stacked rocks but could be permanently demo’ed or opened up as needed.

They head back to the tunnel junction, and head down the other chasm branch, where Aradia detected Unseelie vibes. Feeling, more than hearing, some strange music, Heat starts to dance along with it, though most of the rest of the team resists. Ruxpin is also caught by the song, and they are both lured forward along a quite perilous path, seemingly without realizing how dangerous some of the steps, handholds, and jumps they are using truly are. The rest of the team tries to convince them to stop or slow down, but they are ignored, and quickly lose sight of Heat and Ruxpin around a bend in the tunnel. Those two continue ahead, quickly finding themselves joining a chaotic throng of dancers, all moving to odd, unfamiliar music, seemingly eminating from a castle at the center of what looks to be a medieval-ish town.

They both dance along, joining the crowd, pausing occasionally as their muscles spasm and cramp to drink from some open barrels of some kind of sweet mead scattered around. The rest of the team, worried and unsure what to do, continues advancing slowly. Aradia summons an air spirit to go try to break Heat out of it, who reports back via their astral link about there being some kind of metaplanar crossing ahead, and is itself quickly lost to the dance once it enters and finds Heat. Aradia releases it from service but it seems full under the spell, and remains dancing.

As they reach the crossing, they see an almost seamless transition from tunnel to town, but can see it is all rotted and ruined, strewn with the long and recent dead, as dancers fall away from exhaustion, with fresh ones hurrying to join the queue. The barrels of mead are turned, and sickeningly sweet, and the dancers seem unaware of dangers around them, dancing off the tops of ruined towers as they try to take illusory steps, falling through holes in ruined floors and bridges, etc. The “music” sounds more like the wind whistling through ruined structures and the stamping of feet than anything pleasing. However, Otters start to see the appeal of it all, just for a moment, before Echo gets StepMAMA to blast loud static into everyone’s in-ears, with Aradia commanding them to return.

They rest for a spell, and then realizing that there drugs are starting to wear off, they head back to the van and field hospital.

This seems like a good lead, and Barkins reminds them that ZCorp is a great planar crossroads, so they have high hopes of finding the things they seek without too much trouble, and head out into the ever-present gloaming of the plane, the rain-slick street shining with the reflected lights of the enormous tiers of towers all around them.

With the sheriff now onto them, and clutching his withered hand, PPJ flees up the stairs. Aradia tries to bluff that she wasn’t involved in all the scheming but the sheriff isn’t quite buying it.

Luckily SC has spotted some dynamite in the lockup, and slips in, grabs some, lights it low on the fuse, and shoves it in the back of the sheriff’s armor. This basically blows him in half, also wrecking Aradia’s armor but freeing her from being trapped down here. She also flees upstairs, fearing whatever anti-magic effect is down here. SC stays and continues to fade. Heat rushes down after dodging a shotgun blast and taking out the aged bank teller in response. Outside, the deputies have gotten nervous and started shooting at the welded together buggy car, but Otters starts spinning it, kicking up dust, while TD fires off the flamethrower to discourage them. PPJ quickly takes the deputies out with targeted lightning bolts as he dashes out to the car.

Downstairs, Heat scoops up the strange rock, overcoming a feeling of mundanity and malaise to do so, and then hugs SC a final time as SC disappears into vapor. He dashes back upstairs expecting to make a quick escape, but finds that the team has taken out all visible opposition, as the townspeople hide in fear. They wrap the rock in PPJ’s duster, and tie it 20 meters behind the car, dragging it along as they drive off, just out of range of it’s effects. The mages are disturbed and pissed about what just happened, and Otters is stressed about drastically changing the balance of power by providing this to AZT, concerned it could easily be weaponized. As she sneak drives away to an isolated location, the team gradually talks it through and recognizes that AZT already has a dragon-killing nano-weapon, and ARES already has FAB-III, and other corps have other anti-magic weapons. So while this is surely a powerful artifact, it doesn’t seem likely to trigger a total shift in global power structures.

Thus reassured, they dig a hole and bury it, noting that as with the safe room, the earth packed around it seems to somewhat blunt it’s effect. Thinking about it, the closest thing they know of are astral voids, aka Fovae, but they’ve never heard of those being transportable before, though the rock seems to work in the same fashion. They head back to the City of Steel, having an easier time entering as they have already done the security interview and have their wristbands. They reach M&M, and Aradia heads in first, pissed off, but is slightly confused when the clerks eagerly agree to replace all her lost reagents and only want more details on what occurred. The team debriefs, and provides the location where they buried it to the clerks, who tell them that it sounds like this is the rumored substance known as “void rock” of Fovaeum. They seem very excited to get their hands on some, and quickly agree to upgrade the team’s bands, put them up another night, and at Heat’s insistence, provide some of the local food.

They go back to the bunkhouse to rest, and find a sad stew and old bread awaiting them. Rejecting this, they eat their packed rations instead, and sleep, with a quick convo before where Heat realizes he may have cause SC to fully fade by hugging him with the void rock, but then convinces himself that SC is obviously now living in the void rock, so it’s fine. Unable to sleep, Heat patches some damaged armor and waits for morning. When the rest of the team arises, they find that their upgraded bands have been delivered as promised, and head out to check out the other districts. They find various representations of modern Denver throughout- a tech sector on the rise, various Native American Nations on the borders, the lingering legacy of the divide of the UCAS and CAS, etc, but nothing truly stands out until they reach a heavy security checkpoint into the 7th district.

Unable to pass, they look past it and see the wrecked Tower of the Broken Heart, which looks to have once been three stories, with various atriums and balconies, but to have collapsed in on itself when it split down the middle. It appears composed of hearts made of stone, all cracked, broken, and dripping thick black blood. Various figures are studying it and seemingly attempting various stabilizing rituals- these seem more like material plane mages, and the team surmises this may be another location some of the team’s GW has been sending in have wound up. Not seeing a good way to sneak through or get more intel for now, they decide to call it good on the investigation, they decide to return home, and perhaps return for further work if they can get paid for it. The Detective also announces that they’ll be leaving, retiring from the shadows after an enjoyable dalliance with the team. They will finish some investigations there, and then when they feel ready they plan to return to Motor City, and pick up their old life there- get a new apartment, a new tub, and reconnect with all their old contacts and clients, at least those who survived Bugs and Blackouts. The team is sad to see them go, but this does all make sense, except to Heat, who seems to have a very difficult time saying goodbye. They rest up and prepare to sell their GW paydata to Perri and the COTD, and to figure out next steps for work, new team-mates, and safehouses, as well as determining who to carefully warn about the void rock.

Speculating together, they guess that these Dissonants are using GW"s distraction, bad reputation for caring about civilian safety, and the pre-existing presence of Rifts due to his past with Zebulon as cover for their own Rift experiments, and they guess that the Dissonants are using some random Rifts to sow chaos while also obscuring their true agenda, whatever it is.

As he loses consciousness, he senses a growing burning in his chest- seemingly Thisbe Sorrel being good to her word re: her ritual to deny his body to the Shadow spirits whenever he died.

As he fades into nothing, his last hope is that all the vented oxygen will create some kind of explosion, maybe taking out the baldy or at least doing some damage, but he feels good that at least he didn’t betray his friends….

Worrying!

Otters also feels like her Software skills may come in useful in shaping or manipulating the reality around them.

Aradia “buys” drinks for the house, and the team heads over to that table, with the table turning into a dim corner booth with non-specific anti-surveillance gear as they approach, seemingly their collective vibe for meeting an info source at a dive bar. Knowing that the baldies have access to previously unseen magic, and that they are engaged in metahuman trafficking into Denver, the team is pretty worried about what this may mean…

Feeling they’ve got enough info for now, and noticing Null vines starting to grow through the floor and entwine their legs, they decide it’s time to exit, and beat a hasty retreat to the safehouse, finding themselves once again surprisingly unopposed, though they feel the Null were starting to rapidly catch on to their conning strategies towards the end of their convo. They have a brief confusing time before figuring out how to exit the trick alley that the bar is in, and then a quick walk and drive back to the safehouse, where they easily fall asleep (glad Heat isn’t along with his insomnia as Chiron told them they all needed to sleep at the same time), and awaken in Chiron’s van, still in the forested mountain parkland in Front Range. The smugglers have left with no trouble, seemingly, and it looks like they successfully got the paydata the Johnsons wanted, but what does this all mean for the future of Denver….

Across the Astral Sea

With those caveats in mind, they are welcome to do as they will! Niki requests the team keep this on the DL, even from Cat and other trusted fixers, given the riskiness. They take off, excited to plan a regular old heist.

Cat seems satisfied and explains that even with a ban on spies, it doesn’t mean the spies are gone, and activates a few additional counter-measures to make sure.

She explains the job: she has intel about a secret, likely underground research facility using a meat processing plant as an above-ground cover. She wants to know what they’re researching and whose spot it its, with reduction in pay if either element is undiscovered. Other than getting the info and not getting caught she doesn’t care how they go about it, so long as it doesn’t blow back on her, though the team feels this may be another test of how they operate, and could determine what sort of work she will offer them in the future.

They head back out to the safehouse and rest up, with Creep and Aradia having a weird round of “whatever happened to…” catching up- given what occurred with Carol, Cholula, etc. Aradia watches the Damien Knight snuff BTL, somewhat stunned, and realizes she’s now been in close proximity to two recent AAA CEO assassinations- surely some kind of sign. Creep also notices that Aradia seems maybe a little more pro and a lot less witchy/mall goth, at least at a distance, and Aradia explains that she’s hooked up with some Rogue Lodge agents in town who might be interested in some of the team’s Motor City experiences.

The next day they head out with a lowkey loadout to scope out the meat plant in rural Castle Rock, and find it decently secure but not a super hard target. No obvious sign of a lab entrance or personnel, though the interior security does seem a bit over-equipped and there is a suspicious lack of cameras inside. Aradia and Heat also detect both a bad astral background count and a Dissonance pool, both of which seem to be being created intentionally by making the slaughterhouse layout unnecessarily convoluted and inefficient, causing extra distress to both animals and workers without explicitly doing anything cruel or untoward. A sort of malevolent geomancy.

Disturbed, they decide they need a better path to intel, so Heat, Aradia, and TD all get entry level jobs, which is surprisingly easy given the high turnover rate. Creep stays on-site overnight to keep up surveillance, and makes note of when the plant shuts down, how many people stay overnight, etc. Otters brings the van back the next day with one of the kitted out Mules in the smuggling compartment in case things go hot, and picks up Creep to get his surveillance update. The rest of the team buses in on employee buses from different stops, and gets a brutally short training.

It seems as with the animals, so with the employees- everything is inefficient and slightly dangerous, though not enough so that it would attract particular notice, but would probably drive high turnover. All in all, this seems like an excellent cover facility. Aradia and Heat are also able to ID that the floor of the whole place is both warded and coated in some sort of Faraday material, so they assume the lab is underneath. The one seam looks the be the freight elevator in an obscure back corner, which 2 of the interior guards always have in their LOS.

Heat cuts himself badly later in his shift, and is fired, and told he won’t be paid since his hourly rate didn’t even cover his medical expenses and knife rental, but Aradia performs capably, and TD gets a promotion the big meat saw after they prove very efficient, surprising everyone, even themself. They all exit, and Creep sneaks into the facility amidst the employee exodus after resting all day in the nearby van. He finds a good observation perch, and sees that the interior guards do swap during the overnight, 2 at a time descending the freight elevator and being replaced.

He sneaks aboard and rides down with the second pair to descend, and gets a quick look at the well-guarded foyer at the bottom, before riding back up with their replacements, not wanting to pull a repeat of his and Cholula’s basement adventures in Detroit, since he is getting no comms down here. He stays puts til morning when he can sneak out amidst employee arrival. Meanwhile, TD has put her skills to use and chatted up some fellow workers on the bus, getting some good intel- the inside guards don’t like when people look them in the face, but rotate between a few sets of guards. And more interestingly, rumors are that every friday, some people dressed the same as the other workers but who noone knows ride the buses back into town with everyone else, but don’t come back monday.

With good intel gathered all around, they decide to assess and plan how to gain entry, and Heat purchases some additional hacking shards from Hype in preparation. He’s found himself in a bit over his head- though he hasn’t admitted this to the team, he has primarily gotten where he is now through bluff, guile, an quality implants, and is a little alarmed to find himself having to fully earn his keep, but the pay seems good, and the crew seems “pro”, at least in a way, so he’s in for the ride.

This seems to be a major source of profit for the Ordo, through numerous cutous of course. This seems to have been abandoned to pursue more promising research into “Manifold Levels.”

The funds also seems to be redirected from Taco Temple. implying that the Ordo might be behind that chain as well. So most people who ever ate at TT would likely have some of this neutral but non-passable material left in their bodes! What does the Ordo have planned!

The first are NOX LILITU (seemingly the initial investigation into strange phenomena around Wendigo cults, who are known to eat their followers amongst others, as well as some kind of deal with the Null Sect to assist with the Blackout in exchange for data processing aid). It seems there’s no way Aylin or anyone else could have survived, and they see the villagers scattered off the platform and bridge into the sea as the anchor at the base seems to have severed and the facility is imploding and pulling itself apart.

Upsettingly, the sub is reading a massive radiation spike, though hopefully the water gave them some protection, but they have almost surely come to SK’s attention- they may have to call in another favor from the pirates to escape!

CG has range on the guards, whose high rate of fire miniguns can’t reach his sniper perch, so he contents himself to just pick away at their armor when he can get a shot in, and also provide counterspelling support in case the ritualists get involved, which half of them quickly do. Otters sneaks out of the van, staying in cover, and starts piloting the snake drones into the combat area to attempt some sneak attacks. Dig slips out in animal form and keeps launching spells. Luckily, with the guards gone, they are relatively free to maneuver so Creep gets John Goodman to massively increase his speed and plants all the team’s explosives around the magical barrier, detonating them and cracking it.

As the mages flip between targets, Cholula is badly injured and forced to retreat into the tunnel, while Creep is nearly killed, though John Goodman saves him, pushing him out of sight and getting destroyed in his place. Dig and CG are both targeted and injured, though they manage to stay in the fight with their counter-spelling. With all this distraction, Otters manages to successfully KO a couple mages with the snake drones’ darts- when they lose focus, they themselves are sucked into the ritual and destroyed. It seems to become more chaotic and less stable with each mage lost, but the team doesn’t have a better plan and only intermittent comms so they continue.

Dig is forced to hide himself behind a summoned concrete shield to break line of site as he is almost killed, and then turns to a bug and sneaks into the ritual circle while maintaining his concrete manipulation spell. CG covers him with sniping and counterspelling as best he can. Cholula is badly injured and nearly killed by the mages, who also finally manage to destroy the snake drones with lightning bolts, also nearly killing Otters from the dumpshock. As CG watches his team fall in horror through his scope from far away, Dig makes a last desperate move, pulling on his reserves of good fortune to shape concrete in such a way as to disrupt the ritual circle and it’s runes and markings.

As they start getting hit with the massive drain of the failed ritual, and Dig flees the side effects, the BL mages begin bursting and being sucked into the ritual. Dig is in a weird mental state, seeing as he lost a friend and also a student betrayed him, so he sentimentally holds onto Creep’s meat arm (literally), planning to keep it in the Vault of Ages. Upsettingly, it seems that the walled Casa Aurelius district is now covered in a fully opaque magical barrier, with armed guards patrolling outside.

The team remembers that Freddy Bales introduced them to an older man who he identified as his father at the museum gala in that district, and are horrified to confront the fact that although they were able to halt the main ritual, the threat of the Black Lodge may not yet be over. Passed on CG’s and other scouts’ reports, Ringmaster says they likely have a little time to heal, re-equip, and muster allies, since the BL seems to be on a defensive footing, but that they shouldn’t delay an assault for too long, as who knows what kind of nefarious deeds the BL might get up to in the meantime.

However, some good has come of the team’s actions already- they prevented the primary ritual, and this seems to have closed the Scar, as well as ending the sporadic rifts opening around town. None have been sighted since the ritual was disrupted, and Ringmaster has teams out cleaning up any straggler spirits and making sure their associated rifts close. The spirits seem to all be from the deep metaplanes or beyond- some are what are often classified as “lesser Horrors” or “Tzitzimine.”

The team rests and heals for a few days, with Otters, in a chipper mood as always, sharing memories of Cholula with those who will listen. Marjo-Lin tells Dig that she and some other Keepers were the ones that lured the birdman spirits over to the ritual, having heard Ringmasters call for aid, and also tells Dig she’s sorry for what happened to his magical order- apparently Norman Burger was another one of the BL ritualists! Also, she’s one of The Detective’s close contacts in the Keepers. For now, the team rebuilds and begins to try to figure out what to do about Casa Aurelius- a rich human-centric district makes a lot of sense as a BL stronghold.

It is very creepy, with no bodies in sight, until Smoach zooms in on one of the soldiers checking the body bags, and sees one of them unzip from the inside, from which a corpse sits up and detonates a suicide vest. She also fishes out some dog tags from the creature’s stomach, and everyone else things he must have eaten a soldier, but she explains that swallowing one’s own dog tags is often a soldier’s last desperate act in the face of certain death, hoping that their body can later be ID’ed and perhaps returned to their family. Disturbingly, the tags are neither from the National Guard nor III Corps, but from the Aztlan national army from about 8-10 years ago. Knowles says all of this lines up with her analysis of the other hybrid, though she didn’t retrieve ID from that one. She plays the team a helmet-cam video that the runner team recovered on one of their recon missions, which seems to show III Corp finding themselves enveloped in fog as comms go down, and they come under attack from unknown forces.

She says she also recovered more logs from the runner crew, which she offers to share with the team, but first they brief her on the updates from Detroit- the Scar, the Betas, etc. She is a bit overwhelmed but luckily they confirm that she herself isn’t magical, so she won’t spot Cholula out, while she takes in the info. She seems very serious and driven, but thrown off by her time in the fog- neither of her hardened chronometers are in agreement, and neither align with the team’s estimate of what day/time it is. They decide to rest and patch up the van before heading further in, or bugging out to report what they’ve found so far…..

Regardless, she explains that the real reason she is launching matrix 3.1 (as well as enhanced safety protocols) is because the Foundation has become to dangerous and she wants to get the vast majority of metahumanity further from the NS, to buy some time. She explains that she made a devil’s bargain of sorts with the NS: in exchange for abandoning the Foundation to their control, they won’t expand beyond it, and will limit their attacks to those e-life forms they find especially abhorrent.

She doesn’t trust them at all of course, but thinks this will at least give metahumanity some maneuvering room. She also explains that the CFD/Monad explosion out into the world was of course because of the experiments being done on AI/e-life, but also because something worse was chasing them, so the NS are also partially to blame for that. The team, all sitting back in their seats with their minds blown wide open, agree to potentially look into some of this stuff more, and not spread any of this info wide outside their networks. DDLM offers them significant additional pay for more details about any of this stuff, and suggest they come to her first in the future, as they now have a working relationship, and who knows who else you can really trust?

So they don’t have to specifically target any one agent or even know where they are, so long as they’re somewhat connected to pop cultural norms. The team celebrates their big paydays with some implants and chillin’, closes out a lot of the investigations on their lists, and figures out what to do next.
