Due to the astral patrols around the QZ, it is almost (if not actually) impossible to resummon them while stuck inside. Aseela and AC seem worried, and would like them to look into if they can. They can’t pay much in the way of nuyen, but Toff and Love get the feeling it would boost their rep locally, and might be a good tool in stabilizing the situation a bit (depending on who’s responsible- it could also make it worse!). Love feels especially interested in this mission but can’t quite determine why…

Toff also seems a bit distracted, as it seems he is preparing to initiate, though he is having trouble choosing wether to stick with his current mentor (Oracle) or swap to Dragon, given the power center he is in. He generally seems very open to talking about it though, and Love tries to provide some Wiccan wisdom, giving him a history/cultural lesson in the process. Love’s main advice to Toff is that ultimately power will be the one thing that can help him get where he’s going.

Toff is starting to pick up on how everyone treats Love stange-ly, but he hasn’t gotten to the point of blocking him out yet. Love is trying to stick close, as he also doesn’t know what’s going on. Aseela gives them a few names of people around town to ask about the missing/disrupted allies/free spirits. Toff seems really fascinated with/distracted by Ash, and keeps trying to get him talking more. Ash seems to move around alot, and be a bit paranoid, but generally friendly. Some of the COTD members also treat Ash with a certain reverence…

As time goes on, Toff seems to be making a bit of an effort to avoid Love occasionally, and Love gets a feeling Toff’s been asking around about him- Toff has heard some whispers of some sort of large altercation involving Love shortly after this whole mess began. Toff also has developed a bit of a thing for Ash, and is spending time with him whenever possible. Ash seems both weary and wary of the various politics of the Church, though he seems to know a lot about dragons and their dealings/customs. He warns Toff and Love about some AZT fixers named Sandelerro and Chen who have been working in the area, and are maybe on the lookout for him. Toff also recruits Love to help him try to find Knights of the Dragon members in the Church’s ranks, on Brightwing’s behalf.

In these investigations, Love and Toff do manage to find some people amongst the Church’s followers who seem like they might at least be open to the KOD platform, if not actual members themselves. The idea that a mostly-dead dragon was brought back via some technological means (the current rumor about what’s going on), seems too much like KOD belief to not attract some converts. There is also some discontent in the rank-and-file that Brightwing has been keeping the dragon under such close guard- many believe its Big D come back and want to see for themselves and receive His blessing, while others think it is a new miracle (and time for new leadership!).

Digging deeper into the weird behavior towards Love, Toff questions him. Love doesn’t remember the specific incident that occurred, but tells Toff that he lost some time around when this all started, and hasn’t been able to find his elderly parents anywhere, and fears the worst. Toff decides to leave it at that for now.

Looking into the spirit stuff, they pick up some more rumors and hints, which leads them to a few specific people/places where spirits (and sometimes their metahuman allies) were disrupted/killed. Many of the places have the taint of blood magic, and the names Sandelerro and Chen pop up again as possible involved parties… However, some of the sites have a distinctly hermetic feel, very separate from both the blood tradition, and the Wiccan/dragon magic that suffuses the area. Supposedly some well-armed and armored corp military types were seen in the near vicinity of each attack also.
Love calls a powerful beast spirit to help track culprits in the investigation. Most roads point to the attack originating from a school in Swampscott, and from asking around, they know that the 2 fixers AZT named Sandelerro and Chen are based out of there when in town. Local intel also confirms AJ’s journals that the school is a base of ops for AZT forces in the area. The hermetic attacks are a bit harder to track than the blood magic ones, but still stand out on on the local manasphere (being non-draconic/non-Wiccan), and suggest that someone in the NeoNET camp is likely behind them. You know that Zoh Rothberg, the voice of the great dragon Celedyr, has been coordinating NN activities up here. Ro has an in with her, but they don’t. Zoh’s personal guard all seem a bit strange though- very similar auras/astral signatures. Not quite identical, but abnormally close.

They decide to set a trap for some of the spirit hunters, and recruit Atralchild, Druce and Ash to assist. Using Sanquals as bait, they pick a spot near the water in North Salem (it seems like most of the attacks have occurred when people/spirits were isolated/alone/trying to leave). A hit squad shows up: 4 corpsec goons in body armor and a mage. They spring their trap, and everyone is a little horrified at Sanquals’ massive fireball. Ash explodes another guard, and Toff sees a ghostly draconic mask over his face as he casts, suggesting that Ash may be a drake or dragon, which would explain a lot. Astralchild and Druce take out the remaining guard, while Toff and Sanquals tagteam the mage. Toff mind probes him briefly, and confirms their suspicions: it is a coordinated, multi-corp effort to keep any news from Salem getting out to the QZ at large, or from the QZ out to the world. Whatever actually happened in Boston, the corps are trying to keep it secret for now. They let the mage flee, and confirm that he retreats to the main NeoNET base. So 1 less hit squad, at least. They report their findings, and get paid.

This also seems to help a little bit with Love’s mysterious shunning, as Aseela now at least includes him if not addressing him directly. They decide to look into KOD infiltration of the Church further, and find the most hard core individuals have kind of banded together. Some of the newer converts/possible converts are more vocal than they should be about believing that it is time to overthrow Brightwing, even after Toff warns them off. Many of the suspect people seem merely distrustful of BW’s motives: if it is Big D returned, why won’t she show them? And if not, what is she hiding? Toff doesn’t entirely disagree, but won’t promise to help them either. The runners avoid an outright fight, but it seems they believe that Toff’s loyalties are with BW. Also, they tell him that Love is kind of an out of control caster and killed a bunch of people when this all started, but won’t give more details.

Aseela offers another job, on behalf of Damon: find out who’s been trashing his BAD supplies that are growing along the leyline. The team agrees, and heads down to scout it out. They find some damaged areas with assensing, but have to sneak through anti-dragon Wiccans and Humanis turf to get there, and get spotted before reaching their goal. They kill 3 fanatic Humanis goons and scare off the 3 Wiccan mages with non-fatal wounds. Finding a damaged site along the leyline, they investigate, and find a large amount of evidence pointing at Humanis as the likely funder/culprity, with some Wiccan involvement. Having just trashed 1 group in a hard fight, they decide to hire out the rest of the job, and hire some local entry-level runners who are kicking around to take down as many Humanis chapter members as they can. A dwarf street sam named Halfstack leads the team, and they succeed with light casualties. Toff pays them, and says he’ll be in touch if he needs more work done. Damon offers them free entertainment at his clubs while in Boston (within reason), and also gives Toff a commcode to use to reserve use of Damon’s international collection of safe runner crash pads, as well as a list of cities where they are. Toff is thrilled.

They get a little more info about Love’s background- apparently he’s new to the shadows, and was more of an international pro-Wiccan assassin beforehand. His parents were very involved in Salem, however, and were some of the group of seers who had predicted the coming of a fiery dragon, bearing death and destruction. Many thought that this was Jormungand, during Crash 2.0, and many others later thought it was Damon. But it seems it was most likely the current situation: a reanimated dragon, dripping nanotech. His parents, himself, and many others went out to see what was coming and try to stop if before it reached the town proper, and something went wrong. Somehow, Love channelled far too much mana, and although he somehow survived, everyone (and everything) near him was incinerated, including his parents. But it did help limit the spread of CFD in Salem, and gave the Church people time to start their ritual and bring the dragon down. So people have a complicated view of Love: he killed many, but possibly saved more?

They next investigate the “cure” being offered in Peabody, and find that the area around the town is suspiciously empty of life, and surveilled by drones. As they get closer, they see a bunch of ragers and shamblers acting very strangely- they seem to be on patrol. They don’t have any intelligence behind their eyes, but are moving almost like security drones would. They hide out an astrally project ahead to find out what’s up. It looks like a group of Dissonant Technomancers, possibly even some of the same ones from the train station, have set up shop here, with some large servers and some sort of odd machine-god shrine haphazardly set up in a community center. They also have a bunch of crash beds, where more dissonants seem to indeed be rigging the CFD infected, somehow. They spot Love’s astral manifestatiob, and send the rigged infected after them. They sneak away, luckily not getting spotted, as the security turnout looks intense, and make it back to Salem.

Aseela offers to courier that info (and a general update) to Smedley/Ro, in exchange for Toff filling her in as well, and providing some details about some events in Boston. he agrees, and they trade. Aseela says she had heard rumors that people had been making their way to Peabody and not returning, and that a lot of odd tech had headed that way as well. Also, whispers of the named “Deus”, which she hopes aren’t true…. Aseela seems to have largely gotten over Love’s earlier behavior by now, given the good he’s been doing for the community, and he feels a little better knowing what happened, though not everything is explained: apparently his aura changed a bit after the accident, and it still isn’t clear how exactly he survived.

Toff finally returns to BW to try to make peace within the Church. He tells her she needs to bring the disaffected members in or she will have a revolt on her hands. She acknowledges his point, but says that she can’t: she is choosing the lesser of 2 evils. She says she can’t say more unless Toff initiates, but Oracle warns him to continue thinking critically, and he declines. He makes a deal to hand over the names he gathered and vow his silence, in exchange for a full explanation instead. She reluctantly agrees, and brings him to the gutted basement of the large building they’ve taken over. There, he sees a ritual circle with 12 exhausted high-level Church members on IV’s (and 12 more crashed in beds/pallets around the edges in reserve). Inside is the dragon Eliohann writhes and spits, seizuring wildly and totally out of control.

As Toff watches, the barrier holding him in bulges out under the force of his blows, and it seems the Church barely has him contained. BW says it has been like this since they brought him here from the lake, and that this thing, whatever it truly is, cannot be Dunkelzahn returned. Seeing the nanites crawling over it’s scaled hide, Toff is inclined to agree. However, as BW says, all draconic life is precious, and must be protected, especially as this seems to have some sort of sick corp experiment. She beseeches Toff to keep it secret for now, and try to find out what exactly was done to Eliohann’s body to put it in this state- there are moments where something intelligent seems to take over, but then it slips under again, and worse yet, it is not always the same personality that emerges in these moments.

Toff agrees to research further, and BW gives him the rough locations of 3 ritual sites which she says are linked to this abomination’s creation. She fears the corp’s wanted a controllable dragon, a terrifying thought. She says she can help get him back to Boston proper to look into these sites, and provides Toff with a quiet room where he finally initiates to Oracle, making it official. Although she disapproves of his choice, she respects his intellect. Meanwhile, Love has been doing some serious thinking about his recent past and next steps, and although he is feeling less shunned, he still feels leaving Salem might be best, so he decides to turn to the shadows fulltime, accompanying Toff to Boston.

They accept, and head back into the zone. They reach the pyramid building with no trouble, and find an Aztechnology -sponsored lab complex. They find that the first floor is a museum explaining what is worked on elsewhere in the building: seemingly primarily cultural thaumaturgy and luck magic (on the 13th floor!). They assume lab 15 is likely to be on the 15th floor.

They get in a fight with a rager while headed to the elevators, and come under attack from a trio of spirits who seem to be defending the rager. They defeat them, and deduce that the rager is an infected security guards, and the spirits were most likely commanded to assist them, pre-infection. So they decide to avoid further fights, where possible. The elevators are out, so they take the stairs to the 2nd floor, but decide to grapple up the elevator shaft after sensing some auras further up the stairs. There’s an awful smell when they open the elevator doors, and there seems to be a large corpse pile on top of the car at the bottom of the shaft.

They get up to floor 12, deciding not to risk passing floor 13 in the shaft, as there seems to be some sort of odd magic leaking out of the cracked open door. They take the stairs past 13, with a few of them improbably eating it in the process. They reach the 15th floor, and find the lab they’re looking for, as well as what looks to be the remains of a ritual of some sort. The whole center are of the triangular floor is one large chamber, with a glass barrier that’s cracked and crazed as if from a large explosion of the inside. They head down the hall along one side, looking for an entrance into the lab, when Ro, Toast, and Aemon all drop unconscious unexpectedly. After stim patches bring them to, they figure out that they passed through a mana ward of some sort, and only 2-Chrome (with a high enough force of will) and Senk (non-magical) were able to go through unmolested.

They get to the door, and Senk pops it. They enter, and find an arcane sigil carved into the floor, with the points of the triangle and the pentagram within marked with candles and incense burners. Ro determines that the ritual would have been related to centering and binding something, and the draconic feel in the air, they figure this fits with their emerging theory of what exactly kicked off this whole mess- this ritual would have been a crucial component of merging Cerberus with Eliohann’s body. Toff and Aemon assense, and get some bad vibes- whatever they are, there are 6 of them, and they are not identifiably metahuman. Feeling that her death is near, Senk panics and flees, with Ro trying to talk her down.

Zoh Rothberg says she’ll have explosives ready soon, also, so that’s next on the list after vamps, ghouls, and assassins!

Using a car bomb as an entry point for the Roxxx (and a massive distraction for security) and having the Hellriders ride the nearby roads to try to pull shamblers away, the team manages to reach the facility without attracting attention. They cut through the elecetrified fence (already breached by the Roxxx), and get into the nearby living area, to use internal skyways to get to the labs. They have a few close calls with some staff, but manage to ko everyone quietly.

Senk, using Aemon’s fancy B&E gear, gets them through the security doors, and they drop a few more guards and lab techs, before heading for the nearby emergency stairs that Toff spotted with magic. They find the experimental subjects on the 1st floor, after Toff reads some minds to find out where they are, but are distressed that there are 7 instead of just the 1 kid. Ro, disliking experiments like this one, and Toff, being compassionate in general, start figuring out who/what is in the tanks, and figuring out how to remove them. The rest set traps to hold off guards, while Toast disarms and ties up the guards they fought here.

They plan to free 6 out of 7, finding that one is crawling with nanites. Toff confirms that they seem to be technomancers also. Ro finds a cowering researcher, who helps them free the subjects in exchange for helping her and subject 7 escape- however, she seems to think they already have an arrangement along those lines, which no-one on the team remembers making. Subject 3 says he is almost there and “needs a minute”, but seems to complete whatever he is about quickly. Subject 6, being the healthiest (the advantage of having a relationship with one of the techs), manages to get the elevator working as subject 4 in some sort of feral rage, races off towards the stairs, slowing down the sec forces there further. They finally get everyone else in the elevator just as the sec squad races into the room. They dash out the 2nd floor skyway, the way they came in, and are distressed to see that a large number of shamblers are tearing around the campus, seemingly having gained access through one or both breaches.

They also spot some corpses and destroyed air vehicles in the southern half of campus who seem to have been cut down by the cordon guns: if even corp facilities are targeted, is anyone safe? They manage to flee the way they came, gunning down the shamblers (ragers?) they see on the way without getting grabbed, though they lose a civilian they picked up on the way. They hear some of them mumbling something that sounds like “warn…. cerberus….” Once they breach the fence perimeter, they get wireless back on and flee through the woods. Subject 3 thanks them for the rescue and dashes off in a different direction. They fight off another of the para-cats, which seems to have perhaps become infected also. Toff blasts Ro with a pulse to avoid her catching it too, but fries some of her gear. They receive a message from someone named Nathan Proudfoot, who seems to be subject 3, telling them he has another car waiting for them ahead.

They split up, with Aiden, the ARES kid they are rescuing, driving the new car (which pulls up, parks and opens doors absent Proudfoot), stuffed with people, and the other half of the team making for the team’s car. They make good their escape, and reach the Ancients safehouse at KRB. They contact DJ McCarthy and arrange to drop off the kid, who seems a bit chagrined to have been rescued instead of escaping on his own. He’s very pro-ARES, and loyal to the corp, though he also seems to have a good heart. They drop him off, get paid (most of the way at least) and DJ begrudgingly gives them a contact with a local fixer Smedley Pembrenton III, as they seem to want more money and work. He also asks them to look in on a family member who last he heard was holding the line at Fenway.

They also bring all the remaining techno’s and the tech to a safehouse provided by Viktor Markwart, who offers them sanctuary and instruction. They tell VM about Proudfoot and Aiden as well. He tells them there is useful info and work to be done around town, and they arrange to collaborate on figuring out what is going on. They decide to check in with the fixer next and see what’s cooking. Luckily, Smedley seems to take a shine to all of them, and even provides Chessick with a street name: “Black Sheep”, due to his role in his family, and the fact that the other Black Sheep running in Boston isn’t using the name anymore, as of about 1 week ago. Smedley wants them to raid the Sox trophy room at Fenway, which luckily will also allow them to check on DJ’s cousin, Sarah McCarthy.
Smedley says this a test run to see how the team works together, so he knows what kind of stuff to feed them.

Ro and Toff, who stayed on the southside to work on some stuff, also meet up with the face A.J., who seems to have been imprisoned at the NN facility they raided, having been the leader of the other runner team that the tech was expecting. He used their attack as a cover to escape, and thanks them. They give him some money to get back on his feet (he’s wearing an inside out labcoat currently), and try to figure out why NN left him alive. He tells them that they were maybe just operating on “old Boston” logic- they could have turned him into an asset or made him a company man, the way things might’ve gone before the QZ. Or maybe they thought he knew a way out. Regardless, his team got scattered when he got scooped up on recon for the job that they completed, so he’s gonna go track them down. AJ seems solid, so they agree to stay in touch, after Toff confirms he’s not infected (probably), and he says he will forward them some useful datafiles he’s been compiling and augmenting after inheriting them from their original owner. He is also helping to map all the Catacombs entrances, and offers to give them access to that project if they contribute.

They head over to the stadium, and sneakily approach. They are distressed to discover that not only has the cordon fallen completely, but the stadium is overrun by shamblers, who have amassed a large corpse pile that they are feeding off of in turns. More distressingly, they seem to be erecting some sort of antenna in the center of the field, using girders and damaged pieces from the stadium itself. It looks as if a large number are also directly connected to it in some way. Horrified, they decide to call this one in to someone high up, after they get out. The manage to sneak up to the trophy room undetected, but find a group of survivors holed up inside under siege from a group of shamblers.

They kill (or at least incapacitate) the shamblers, and free the survivors: Sarah, a DocWagon dwarf named Musa Matevosian and his injured colleague, a reporter named Allison Sanborn, and a young girl named Jane. They notice some bodies in the corner, and Toff tells the team he’ll carefully assense everyone for infection after they escape. They enlist the survivors’ help in grabbing trophies, and hightail it out of there, after realizing they’ve been made. They manage to avoid any serious entanglements, and arrange to meet DJ and pass off the rescued individuals.

Sarah seems pissed that the UCAS FBI has taken over the investigation into what went on, and her and Allison show the team footage of the military and feds pulling back from the Fenway cordon, leaving KE to get overrun. Sarah vows to continue digging, feds or no, and thanks the team, as does DJ, begrudgingly. Allison asks to stick with them, as they seem like they’ll lead to some good stories. Musa and his colleague take off with the McCarthy’s, but he gives the team his comm in case they need medical. jane seems to have bonded to Chessick a bit, and she also wants to stick with them. Toff starts telling her about his religion on the way over, but kind of terrifies her with his description of a ghostly dragon god watching everything. Ro contacts Zoh Rothberg to warn her of the Fenway antenna, and she says she will confirm and respond. She seems a bit haughty but has the most beautiful voice Ro has ever heard. Ro also leaves a message with Erika Knowles, the Boston OSI head, to offer the team for work.

They reach Smedley’s, and sell him the gear. Disturbingly, Jane turns out to be a technomancer, which she reveals when she mindfries a small surveillance drone that someone snuck into Smedley’s secure area. He says he thinks it is probably The Dragonslayers, a gang from across the harbor that has been creeping onto his turf and causing trouble, as well as kidnapping locals. He asks them if they want to leave Jane in his care, promising to see to her training and watch her back, and they agree after some debate if she should go to Markwart instead. She prefers Smedley, as it seems likely she’ll see the team more here.

The team also plans to use Jane’s grandfathers’ house as a potential safehouse, assuming it is actually empty, as it is in a nice ‘hood. Allison is hitting on Senk quite a bit, who doesn’t know how to respond, and ignoring Aemon hitting on her/trying to impress her. They leave Allison and Jane in the Leather District after stocking up on armaments at Legit’s Weapons near the LD entrance to the Catacombs. Having been warned repeatedly not to run afoul of Mama’s Boys, they stay out of trouble while on their turf.

They link back up with the Ancients, and rig up their car as a full-on battlewagon, with a turret gun, armor plating, a cowcatcher, and expanded interior space. They accept Smedley’s next job: to look into the Dragonslayers and teach them a lesson. Ro insists on riding her chopper, even though she could fit in the car. They pay tolls to the Mama’s Boys to use the big dig tunnel across the harbor, and emerge in Iron Wolves turf. Toff feels a sensation while underground, and confirms that there is a dragon leyline, which they seem to have crossed. They notice a pack of chromed riders following them, and Ro rolls out to meet the leader after he demands a “test of strength”. They tie one arm together, and begin fighting. Ro gets first blood, before being injured herself. This seems to satisfy the pack, as the leader gives her a hard sniff and then releases her, and the CW’s ride off. Ro is thrilled.

They reach DS territory, and assense a large crowd gathered nearby. Heading there, they round a corner and find about 20 gangers outside of a pretty trashed-looking bar. Toast sneaks onto some nearby roofs but the rest of the team is easily spotted, given their conveyance. They pull up out front and Chessick steps out to try his social magic. The DS’ers are having none of it, and one of them tries to stab him. Luckily he dodges, and the DS’ers don’t seem to really be prepared for a throwdown with runners, as they make short work of them, killing or ko’ing a bit over half before the others flee. They grab 3 of the ko’ed, and Toff mind probes them while they race away, fearing heavier reinforcements.

They find out that the DS’ers boss is a newish member named Luna, who seems to have used some mind control to ascend the ranks, and also discourage talking about her. She is a vaguely Mesoamerican-appearing human. Her HQ seems to be an abandoned Stuffer Shack near the hospital, as this is where the kidnapping victims are brought. However, none of the gangers know what happens next, or seem to want to: they all seem a bit scared of Luna. The team reports to Smedley, and he pays them a bit for what they’ve uncovered, and spurs them to keep digging. They decide they might as well track down Luna while they’re already in the area, so they head back to DS turf, where Ro and Chessick plan to do a series of distracting drive-by’s while Toff, Senk, and Aemon sneak up to the target building.

Meanwhile, Toast has slipped off to do some investigation of his own. He noticed that some of the elves amidst the DS-er’s they threw down with had some old-school IRA tat’s that looked alot like O’Connor’s pre-TRC force insignia. Needing to know more, he followed some of the injured and fleeing members back to another safehouse, where he found that some of the DS LT’s are, indeed, terrorists wanted by Tir na nOg. However, they seem to have been pushed aside or demoted a bit under Luna’s leadership. They have an old-school IRA style, and remind Toast of some of O’Connor’s loyalists from the 40’s. He decides to keep digging before acting, and scouts out an escape route for the team.

The drive-by’s go fine, initially hitting some smaller targets before the HQ. However, the HQ guards prove to be better armed and manage to shoot out the engine block on the battlewagon. Chessick lays down suppressive fire, forcing them into cover, as Ro tries to strategize. The back team almost gets spotted a few times, and finds a watcher spirit following them, which Toff easily destroys. Disturbingly, it seems to have been summoned by a blood mage, so they prepare for trouble. They enter the rear of the HQ with a crowbar just as Ro comes under attack by a massive manifested blood spirit inside the car.

After an extensive gunfight with a few regular gangers and a few elite guards in back, the team heads out front to try to help Ro and Chessick. Toff goes astral from the back alley to attack the spirit on 2 fronts, and summons a guardian spirit to assist. Luckily, this assault prevents the spirt from draining much of Ro’s essence, though she looks a bit pallid and aged when she emerges from under its spell. Toff deals a mighty blow, but is ko’ed himself, only saved from death when his guardian spirit (who he has been plying with reagents, and who seems to view this as a worthy fight) sacrifices itself to save him from the mortal blow. The spirt manifests and sends Aemon fleeing in terror. Senk manages to destroy it with a well-placed series of grenades however. The team links back up and starts working on healing, before realizing they left Toff out back.

They race around the rear to find Luna and 2 more elite guards absconding with Toff’s limp form. After an epic firefight, and much damage to all involved, they manage to fell them all and secure Toff (Aemon is almost crushed cathing his falling form as Luna was midair with Toff’s body when she died). They heal Toff up real quick, and he manages to probe Luna’s brain before she fully dies, further injuring himself in the process. But they get the name of her boss: Cruzado. This is who she has been delivering the kidnapped people to. So they have the lead they need. They quickly investigate the SS interior, and finding nothing especially valuable or suspicious (it seems Luna was trying to keep her blood magic on the dl, and had merely been using her mind control spells her, as well as temporarily storing the kidnapped people), they flee back towards the Leather District, in a car that it turns out Jane is remote-controlling under Smedley’s instruction.

As they pass through the DS/Iron Wolves border, they see they Wolves have already started tagging over some DS stuff and claiming turf, and hear a distant howl. Ro howl’s back, surprisingly convincingly! They pay the tolls to the Mama’s Boys, feel the brief zazz of the Dragon Leyline again, and safely reach the Leather District, though it appears the District has come under attack while they’ve been away. Once they heal up a bit and are all conscious, Smedley tells them the tale: apparently around the time that the team attacked the HQ, a group of ragers burst out of a previously unmarked Catacombs entrance under a shack in the district, and started wreaking havoc. Luckily a good amount of citizens have been getting a bit of training from Buster’s Militia, and the resident runners and spellcasters managed to hold them off. Toff goes to investigate a bit, and confirms that all the attacker’s bodies in the burn pile are infested with nanites, and also that many of the kidnap victims seems to be amongst their number.

There is also a large group of mages enacting some sort of ritual to seal up the Catacombs entrance, as there are apparently quite a few more ragers still inside. Smedley says the Mama’s Boys have claimed that this underground area is not part of the Catacombs proper, and thus not their direct concern/responsibility, id’ing it as The Labyrinth, a series of tunnels, chambers, caves, etc under the Boston Commons. Smedley lets them rest up in his safehouse and hang with Jane a bit while he digs into Cruzado. He has info within a day, but they aren’t ready to roll for a few. Many members of the team are approached by a kind of creepy dwarf named Bozeman, always accompanied by a few small drones, who wants to hire them for some wetwork jobs. Toast has worked with him before, and they tell him they’ll be in touch if interested. He says it’s a good time to be in the biz as a lot of folks are using the QZ as an excuse to settle scores and clean house.

Aemon is also approached by a strangely familiar man that he doesn’t recognize, who introduces himself as Thankyou, and seems disappointed that Aemon is a bit creeped out. He repeatedly dodges the question of why he is in a different body now, and mostly wants to gets updated on the team and talk about the Gilgamesh Initiative job he wants to hire them for. He says he came here in person since comms haven’t been getting in and out, and thought it would be good to have eyes on for the job at hand. Aemon tries to avoid letting TY touch him, and says he’ll be in touch, but returns to the team thoroughly disturbed. They debate a bit about what to do, but don’t come to any firm conclusions other than maintaining a physical distance.

Finally all healed after a few days, they head to the Stuffer Shack that Cruzado seems to manage, in Backbay, near the water. They find it gutted and burned, with a charred corpse pile inside. Assensing it, Toff gets both some bad new vibes, and some bad longterm vibes. Scouting around, Chessick finds some pleasure-craft in the nearby marina, 1 of which has an intact security cam on it. He gets some footage, and they see a group of heavily armored corpsec types roll up and systematically execute everyone in the place, before torching it. The one exception is Cruzado, who Toff recognizes from Luna’s mind, who they bind and bring out front just as a handsome man on a fancy motorcycle pulls up. He says something to Cruzado before signalling the guard. The guard double-taps Cruzado, and the man speeds off as the corpsec finishes the burn prep. They save the video and have to pull Ro away from the boats to go investigate the wreckage.

Digging through, they find a secret basement area, which looks to be old smuggling tunnels, maybe from prohibition days or earlier, cut into the bedrock and emerging from a false sewer grate onto the river. The facility is completely flooded now, but they find a bit of info amidst the ruins- it seems like some kind of self-destruct sequence was activated, likely by Cruzado or the corpsec, which Ro has ID’ed as Aztechnology based on arms and armor. Toff, levitating about to stay just above the slightly shimmering water in the cramped tunnels, finds 4 corpses: all kidnap victims, they seems to have been stored here after Luna delivered them, and drowned when the self-destruct was activated. He also finds some containment chambers, now broken, and some canisters labelled Project Vulcan that look to fit perfectly in an injection port on the side of the chambers. He assumes this is where the nanites in the water came from, and likely why all the kidnap victims seems to have become infected, though how/why they ended up in the Labyrinth is a mystery.

They return to Smedley with this info, get paid, and plan their next job. Lucky Liam calls with some urgent work for the O’Rilley Mafia that the Ancients are in charge of seeing done. Erika Knowles, with the OSI, calls Ro back and tells them their is a job investigating some sort of Atlantean Foundation ghost ship that slipped into the harbor just ahead of the cordon going up, but which no one has heard from and no one has gotten off of. Zoh Rosenberg calls, and Ro once again loses herself in the beauty of her voice, as she offers to provide ordnance for the team to take out the shambler antenna at Fenway. Plus, Bozeman’s and TY’s jobs: plenty of work!

Team 2 Part 6

Shri decides to hold off on deciding what to do with Achilles’ recent betrayal until the rest of the team returns. Munty and Twitch both fly back in from NYC, having completed their jobs there. They decide to call it water under the bridge, in that it happened, but seems not to have had severe consequences for them as of yet. Achilles agrees to acquire some Laes from his Tir contacts, and to keep a dose in his auto-injector, and 1 in his false tooth, so that he can erase his recent memory if he gets captured again (or gets ko’ed on a run). They also track down an old and abandoned firehouse to rent as the new Safehouse. They kit it out a little bit, and set Servaas up as the safehouse master (for now) to give him something to do, which it seems like might help him. They also establish some common rules, which is basically don’t come there if you are being followed, and don’t bring civilians around (other pro’s is ok, using discretion). Munty is excited about the prevalence of rats to feed/befriend. The build-out on the space should be done by the time they finish their next job: using the info they received from Izidor Kurtlanik to finally get revenge on Theo Two-Hearts!

They head to the Rhino to meet Bug, and find a grizzled man in his 50’s with an air of both competence and quiet desperation, wearing a fringed armor jacket and generally looking straight outta the 2050’s. Munty tries to rifle through his pockets, but he catches her doing so, and they have an awkward few first minutes. However, Servaas vouched for both sides, Bug needs work, and he’s a skilled spirit fighter and hunter/tracker, so he seems like a good guy to have along on the job. They agree to terms, and report to Pia Oliversson that they’re ready to move on it. She gives them a little bit of job money, as she’s also pissed at Two-Hearts for burning her. She is similarly unhappy with Achilles.

They contact Blackhawk to run them across the Sioux border again, and he agrees, for a severe discount, as Two-Hearts trashed his safehouse. Clippy does some matrix recon, and finds out that Two-Hearts now holds dual Sioux/ Evo Corporation citizenship, and resides on a secure research facility way out in the boonies. Supposedly, this facility is dedicated to food research, but rumors on the matrix point to other experimental biotech taking place there, and possibly even a wing dedicated to figuring out what is going on with CFD. Bug sends a spirit scout ahead, who confirms that Two-Hearts is on the base, as they fly over in BH’s Osprey. BH and Achilles bound over their common military background, and Twitch (using his action hero persona) tries to join in, but is unable to convince them (as he mostly remembers training montages, and tragic battlefield deaths of a series of best friends and lovers).

They parachute down a ways out from the facility, and make their way on foot the rest of the way, using their high plains ghillie blanket from the last Sioux run to provide some concealment as they near. Spotting drone security, and deducing that the base probably uses a “safe target” IFF system, they decide to wait on the access road and ambush a car coming up, to hopefully get some RFID tags to mark themselves as “employees”. Shri plays an injured traveler, and cons a car into stopping. Bug, Achilles, and Twitch kill the 3 men inside, grab their RFID’s, and hide the bodies under the ghillie blanket, off the road a ways. Clippy and Achilles conceal themselves in the back of the jeep, while Twitch drives and Shri and Munty ride upfront (with the 3 chips). Bug stays outside with a sniper rifle to provide cover as needed.

They drive up to the base’s entrance, and Shri manages to con her way past the Evo Marine guard at the booth, distracting him while Clippy qucikly adds her name to the pre-approved list. They enter, and park briefly in the lot, while Bug sends another spirit to locate the target. The spirit guides them towards him in astral space, with Munty navigating. They find Two-Hearts surrounded by 4 Evo Marines in a farm field, with a large number of farm drones clustered around them. These drones, as well as the security drones, seems to have disconnected themselves from the WAN, and seem to be self-upgrading. Clippy is disturbed, but also fascinated, and Munty wants to flee, but holds it together. As they pull up, they see Two-Hearts unplugging a data-cable from the nearest farm drone.

Meanwhile, Bug has been trying to sneak around the base in the flat plains, and gets spotted and ko’ed by a security drone. Luckily, his spirit was still around, and comes to the rescue, concealing him and hauling him away from the combat zone. Twitch guns the car towards Two-Hearts and the Marines, who all dive aside in a disturbingly synchronized fashion. He rams the farm equipment instead, slightly damaging the Jeep, but trashing many of the drones. Achilles jumps out and slices one of the Marines with his monofil whip, before bieng ko’ed himself by the Marine’s shotguns. They get in a drawn-out and brutal fight- the Marines keep rising again after they think they’ve put them down, after twitching and writhing on the ground: something is definitely wrong here.

They finally get a solid hit on Two-Hearts, who seems to snap out of a trance as he looks around him. He seems very surprised to see them and asks what they are doing there, and says they have to help him escape- something is wrong with him! They refuse and shoot him again, which seems to cause a personality switch. They briefly discuss grabbing him to take him with, but after Twitch sees how much blood is all over his body already, he decides against it and caves Two-Hearts skull in with his own ancestral tomahawk. They load up into the Jeep and race towards the fence as the security drones finally turn on them en masse (Clippy has been slowing them down via hacking).

Twitch rams through the fence, but heavily damages the Jeep in doing so, between the electrical charge and the impact itself. Achilles suppressive fires out of the rear of the vehicle to try to keep the drones and remaining marine back. They’re worried they aren’t going to make it, when Blackhawk’s Osprey suddenly drops in before them and opens up on their pursuers with a gatling gun. BH also seems to have winched up Bug’s body while security was distracted, so they race aboard, and Achilles stuffs the tomahawk into his smuggling compartment to reduce the chances of being magically tracked. They race for the border, taking a more circuitous route than on the way in to avoid any heightened security.

They arrive safely in Seattle, and return to their new safehouse- Munty has a small dugout (perhaps the beginning of a proper warren?) and with Rat’s help, uses her recent experiences to gain the ability to focus her magic and transform into a rat form. Shri relaxes in her private “panic room” which she pays extra for. Achilles and Twitch both feel like it might be a good idea to get scoped out by a street doc or something, to make sure they didn’t catch anything, as they were right up in the thick of it, and got spattered with quite a bit of biological material during the firefight. Next up: time to make some money!!

Midair Massacre
9/20/2015, 2:20:22 AM
Runners:
Hacking Crew:
Munty

Sem-par
and introducing Clippy

Munty

The team from the archive job meets up in the Underground, with the help of the Rat Pack, and reaches a safehouse in Terminal. Munty and Ro join them. After Aemon awakens, and is assensed by Toff, he confronts Ortega about how he survived. Ort confirms that he gave Aemon some ghoul blood, in order to save his life/soul. Aemon tells him that he did a good job, and says Scorpion Gallery Scarf, detonating Ort’s head bomb. The Rat Pack charges them extra for the mess. They also are contacted by the Catholic Church and by Vasuda Mueller, requesting Ortega’s remains. They decide to give them to the Ghoul Liberation League, who say they will venerate them appropriately, and pay a small sum. Aemon and Ro also manage to track down the NYC branch of The Continental with Sully’s help, having found a strange RFID chip on Ortega. They also find out that they are the executors of Ortega’s will- which primarily leaves his amassed fortune to the GLL with a significant donation to Aemon’s Kids. The remaining team accepts another job from One, and hire a bunch of out of town hackers to do the first stage. Munty helps SP and Rudd sneak onto an airport to gain access to classified flight transponder codes for a private corp flight out of SeaTAC. Clippy and Drekbomb provide support from offsite after grid-hopping over. They gain access to the backup flight support facility, and get the codes while Munty ko’s the few wandering security guards who get too close. They manage to exfiltrate without getting snagged, and SP and Rudd make their return flight to Hamburg. Munty heads out to Buffalo with Chessick in tow (who has discovered some tantalizing hints about the hunt for Atlantis on the extra drive he grabbed at the Vault), and meets up with the rest of the team.

They have managed to convince and old dwarf rigger, Wheels, to come out of retirement for “one last job.” Luckily he still has all his rigger gear, and has been aching from some action. They are supposed to pull off his “signature job” again: a midair extraction. One wants them to get 4 corp execs, and kill everyone else in an “accident” to cover it up. They spend a few days tooling up an old plane Wheels has handy, camouflage it as best they can. Using the transponder code and flight info, they plan to intercept right after the corp flight crosses the Sioux border back into UCAS. Wheels buys some insulated, bulletproof bodybags from Team Zero to keep the execs safe during the extraction.

They take off, and cruise high up while Chessick uses the transponder codes to hack into the flight controls. After taking control, they descend both flights to a lower altitude, and get into a holding pattern nearby, before launching over on the glider sled. They magnet on, cut through the hull, kill the pilots and guards, and manage to (barely) zipline the 4 execs back to their plane, where Chessick and Munty catch them. Chessick codes a new flightplan to send the corp plane into Lake Michigan just past Chicago, figuring that Bug City is a good cover for a mysterious accident.

They split off, and return to Buffalo, where there is a group of Red Dragon Triad goons waiting. They provide the pay, and leave with the execs. The team celebrates at Wheels’ nearby bar, and starts planning how to get into Boston. Vault Hunting

After the success of the last job, One hires the team again for a heist. They seemed to have gained some face, as One treats them with noticeably increased respect. One, once again, provides a detailed dossier on the target: the main city of New York data archives, in a secure offline vault storage system under the city center library. It uses wi-fi negating wall treatments, but the magical security seems light- mostly focussed on detection and reporting of magical threats, rather than actual counter-measures.

Toff, using his MIT&T grad student SIN, accesses the vault as a “legit” user, to check the protocols, and seeing the difficulty of access they decide they will need 2 things: a large shaped charge, and a distraction. Luckily, Prometheus Engineering, which built the library and vault (as well as many of the other spaceage structures in Manhattan) also provides security. And they have an additional office building/warehouse next door. The 2 building’s security teams act as backup for each other until NYPD INC shows, and the security spiders for both bulldings share an office next door.

So the plan is: Aemon and Ortega will steamroll into the office building, and using non-lethal ammo and gas grenades, neutralize any guards they encounter (and hopefully the spiders), which should call the library guards over. The rest of the team will have entered the library ahead of time, with a large C4 charge concealed in Twitch’s cyberleg smuggling compartment. Toff will conceal them using spellcraft, while they sneak downstairs, and re-route the hardwired alarms. Then they will attempt to bypass the physical locks to get to the final vault door, which they will blow (the sound of which Toff will also conceal). They will use a pre-summoned spirit to grab the drive they need, and sneak back out, hopefully exiting the building amidst a crowd if any patrons haven’t been cleared out yet. They also get a side job from Sully to swap one drive with another provided by a client.

Toff (invisible) goes ahead to spot cameras/sensors, while Twitch and Chessick trail behind, disabling them. They reach the sub-basement door, and disable that alarm as well. They find the electrical room without encountering any guards, and Twitch and Chessick prepare to re-route the alarms as soon as Ort and Aemon start the distraction. Toff stays on astral/clairvoyant overwatch.

Meanwhile, Aemon and Ort, having finished their street food, enter the office building, and using SNS rounds, ko the guard at the desk, and dash through the security sensors, setting off a series of alarms in the process. They race up the fire escape (more alarms) as panicked employees try to flee the other way. They don gas masks, and ko another guard on the way to the top floor. They loose some gas grenades, and ko the remaining 2 guards, who only manage to hurt them a little. However, the spiders have locked their room down, and Aemon is heavily injured by a drone turret firing SNS back at him. They destroy the turrets, but can’t find a way in. So they content themselves with chucking more gas grenades from the windows at the arriving security from next door.

Back at the library, with the signals re-routed, the team heads back up a floor, disabling a final fire alarm, before sneaking towards the vault as they hear the guards heading up in the elevator, and a PA alarm instructing all patrons to head to the 1st floor, where library staff can keep an eye on them until the security situation is dealt with. Through a combo of technical ability and magic, they manage to imitate the procedure that Toff observed and gain access to the main vault, without setting off any alarms or traps. They place the charge and blow the door. However, Twitch overdid it a little bit, and the blast, the rapid exit of all the air in the room, and the shrapnel cloud nearly kills Chessick. Luckily, Twitch snags him with a grapple gun before he gets sucked through the hole and falls to his death. Toff heals him up magically, and Twitch and the spirit enter to grab the drives.

Aemon and Ort decide to flee, but find that the spiders seems to have locked the building down, with security shutters over man doors. They manage to pry and squeeze their way through, but lose 1 gun and their crowbar in the effort. They jump out a back window on the 2nd floor, to head to their Underground entrance/escape route, where their Rat Pack contact awaits. They are spotted by some civilians, some of whom scream, flee, film them, or call for help. They dash off on foot, but are quickly overtaken by 2 cop cars. They race for the sewers, but Aemon is killed by a shotgun blast after firing at one of the cars. Ortega scoops him up, and dives in, as the Rat Pack drags a cover over. Fearing for his friend’s life (and immortal soul), Ortega massages some of his blood down Aemon’s throat, returning him sputtering to life (though only just).

The rest of the team, having retrieved the drives with no trouble, manages to join the milling patrons as they are escorted from the building (as the explosion appears to have set off a seismic sensor, and the spirit some sort of astral intrusion alarm). With Toff maintaining their invisibility spells, and some lucky sneaking, they escape the police cordon that is hastily being established, and rendevouz with their own Rat Pack escape route a short ways away. Twitch grabbed 1 extra drive, so they have 1 mystery drive for Sully’s client, 1 for themselves, and the sole master copy of the blueprints of NYC for One. Now they just have to escape through the treacherous tunnels of the Underground.

A Manhattan Project
8/10/2015, 4:23:02 PM

Ro Tain returns to Renraku’s warm embrace to “upgrade her body”, they have apparently made some advances since she was initially grown. They link up, and get kinda weirded out by Twitch, who asks to stash a large load of BTL’s in their van as well. They receive a message from a local fixer named Sully offering them a ride into town, and some help navigating Manhattan’s peculiarities. As Sully claims to know all the best spots, and they are early for the meet, Chessick gets him to drop by a quality back alley suit place, and get his armor repaired as well as some new duds. They head to the meet, at a bar called Contents Under Pressure. Weirdly, they have a window for the meet rather than a specific time. They get in with no trouble as they left all their weapons behind, and grab a table. However, they all get distracted or approached by various parties, including some agonizing college philosophers, a recent divorcee, a gigolo on the prowl, and a wine snob. Managing to control their tempers and navigate some social situations, they wait around for the Johnson, though their suspicions are somewhat aroused by the unusual forwardness of the patrons. Munty picks some pockets, but failing to find anything good, gives up and sleeps under the table for a bit.

After and hour has passed, they are ushered into a back room by an apologetic server, where an Asian man in fatigues with a 58th Battle Brigade unit patch brings them through a secret door. They find themselves in a loading dock, surrounded by more mercs, with a table set in the middle of the room. Across the table are 3 people: a large female African troll carrying a drone, a surprisingly-aged Asian elf man in a robe covered in Wujen symbols, with glowing eyes and lightning crackling from his fingers, and an Asian man who looks like a classic suited gangster. The gangster type ushers them over and tells them to sit. Chessick inquires what was up with that stuff in the bar, and the man half smiles and says it was “merely a test.”

After some cryptic negotiation of terms and pay, they introduce themselves as One, and explain that they are hiring on behalf of the Red Dragon Triad. They want to subsume the local Big Circle Triad into their organization, and want the team to blackmail 3 of the more vulnerable council members. As long as they convince all 3 to cooperate, or convince 2 and kill 1, before the end of the week, they will be paid in full and potentially offered further work. They receive a dossier on the targets, and get to work. After some B&E and some social engineering, they convince the first target to cooperate by securing surveillance of her communicating with the Triad, and threatening to alert her employers at Zurich Orbital Bank to her affiliations. Being a logical type, and seeing that she is a bad spot, she agrees. Twitch creeps everyone out a little by switching back and forth between a wannabe romantic comedy character and a noir detective persona during the run. Onto the next target!

They decide to have Twitch stay and watch the safehouse during the next leg, as he seems to have defaulted to his base “blank” state and is weirding everyone out. Sully messages Ortega that there are some of “his people” in a community in The Pit, after dropping Ort off near The Continental, and seemingly discerning his purpose/true nature despite his disguise. Ort decides to check it out while the rest of the team recons the next 2 targets. He gets to the Pit with no trouble, and follows his nose once inside. However, he fails to scare off some local ganger youth after misplaying his attempt to intimidate, and decides he better teach one a lesson. Before he knows it, he has caught and is devouring the youngest one, a boy of about 12. Horrified at his harming of a child, he panics, and Aemon has to talk him back to the safehouse, where he decides to lay low for a while.

The rest of the team checks out the second target, a talismonger with Aztechnology ties. Munty scopes out his shop, and spots a back room where it looks like the real deals go down, as the front is mostly tourist trinkets and some basic reagents. She buys an enormous quantity of rabbit’s feet as a cover, and leaves. Aemon mails them to Aemon’s Kids as a gift, along with a carton of smokes. They decide that Chessick (acting as a dilettante) and Aemon (his bodyguard) while distract the mark and get him out of the shop, while Munty infiltrates and sets up some surveillance gear. Chessick convinces him and his girlfriend to hit the clubs (on Chessick’s dime) and they close up early. They go to a Triad club, but Aemon is able to confirm via Jackpoint that it is neither Big Circle nor Red Dragon operated: a good first component for the blackmail.

The talismonger procures some drugs from a source at the club, who he seems to be steeply in debt to. He gets Chessick to overpay, paying down his debt a bit, and they all slam back a small vial. Chessick is forced to astrally perceive for the first time ever, and spends hours dancing, before Aemon makes him vomit to try to get him out of there (after the mark leaves). Chessick keeps tripping for hours though, and has a nasty crash afterwards, as well as terrifying dreams of shadowy forms trying to grasp him. He wakes up wanting more, desperately, and Aemon, with some research, is able to confirm that he has become addicted to tempo, an incredibly dangerous drug with some nasty side effects. However, they got good blackmail info.

Meanwhile, Munty infiltrated the shop (using biometrics that Chessick had hacked in) without a hitch, and plants the cameras. She tries to steal another rabbit foot on the way out, but almost sets off a motion detector and bails instead. They decide to leave the cameras to gather more evidence for another day or so while they check out target 3: a Renraku Computer Systems security officer. His only vulnerability (as he lives where he works, at a secure Renraku complex) is his daughter, who attends a prestigious private girl’s school downtown. They decide to take a 2-pronged approach, so Chessick hacks her social media profile, figures out how to copy her writing style from some old assignments, and forges some heavily plagiarized work for her upcoming assignments, explicitly violating the school’s code of conduct. He sets a data bomb inside, to delete the files if the father cooperates.

That night, Munty sneaks past the school’s security, while the rest of the team provide matrix, astral, and physical overwatch, and gains access to the girl’s room. She takes a picture of her gloved hands “framing” the sleeping girl’s face, and then plugs into her commlink, which Chessick hacks and uses to submit the plagiarized assignments. Munty can’t resist stealing some ice cream from the dorm room fridge, and slips while climbing back out the window and trying to eat it at the same time, falling into some shrubs below. Luckily, she manages to slow her fall and creep off before security responds, though it does look like she woke up the people in the room she left as well.

They call the father from their doss in Terminal, and give him the terms: he will cooperate or they will get his daughter expelled. They send the pic Munty took to get his attention, and prove they can get to her when/should they need to. He grunts and angrily tries to argue but Chessick shuts him down, having correctly surmised that attending this school will be a major social step up for the next gen of his family, and that he is unwilling to compromise. He agrees to help, although he says that they have greatly dishonored him, which Chessick scoffs at. They bail on Terminal, in case the sec officer tracks them, and head to The Pit to try to crash with the ghouls. They find the Ghoul Liberation League compound without any trouble, and arrange to rent a safe room there for the next few nights. Ort is summoned upstairs to meet their leader, Vasuda Mueller.

She tells him that his actions of a few nights previous have caused some problems, as the GLL has a carefully negotiated arrangement with the other denizens of The Pit. Eating children on the street is not how they do things here. He apologizes, and she tells him that it would be a shame to have to throw him in with the ferals in the underground. Ort takes the hint and promises to behave. She also says that given his situation (i.e. the bounty) it would be best if he laid low, as she doesn’t want any trouble for her people, though she appreciates his True Communion teachings. He tells her he is only passing through town.

They decide to retrieve the gear from the talismonger’s, and Munty sneaks back in while Ort provides lookout, while Chessick and Aemon go back to the same bar to meet up with the proprietor again. They quickly review the footage, but don’t find any further incriminating evidence- it seems like he runs the shop pretty clean, and mostly keeps his habits on the sidelines. So Chessick lays it out with what they have: he is addicted to a notoriously dangerous, unstable drug, and is in debt to dealer’s working for a different Triad, all of which Big Circle would frown upon. The mark agrees to swap loyalties, on the condition that Chessick gets Red Dragon to square his debts and allow him to do as he pleases with his free time. Chessick runs it by One, who agree, and confirms.

With that completed, they accept a final small task from One, and deliver some sort of message scroll to the Big Circle Triad’s incense master at his fancy penthouse. The rest of the council is also there- the sec officer staring daggers at them, the talismonger casually greeting them, and the auditor avoiding their eyes. The fact that runners, rather than Red Dragon Triad members, delivered this message is a calculated insult (and perhaps the real message) to remind the BC of their new place as RD subsids. They leave, before any trouble starts, having succeeded in not doing anything grossly inappropriate. Ort receives a call from Vasuda, who tells him her sources say that some Euro types have been asking after him around town. The team decides not to go back to the GLL place, in case it’s being watched, and accept another job from One, which includes a decent hotel in the pay. This time, they’re going to break into the ultra-secure offline archive and steal the master blueprints for NYC!

The team, holed up in their Ork Underground safehouse, is getting antsy, and wants to start looking for revenge. Achilles tries to cheer one man up, but ends up creeping him out worse maybe, before he is torn apart by a pack of awakened coyotes.

Shri, in the crowd, notices some ascetic looking cyber-warriors taking note, and hopes for the best. Both Achilles and Twitch find invites to join S.y.A in their gear back in the locker room, and after splitting the purse with Shri, head to the arranged meet. Shri sneaks up and hides nearby, not being invited herself. They find a group, mostly orks and humans, all dressed in urban camo and well-armed, and all sporting a fair amount of ’ware.

The leader introduces himself in a light Aztlaner accent as “El Comandante” and offers them entry, if they pass his test. He summons 2 burly orks forward, who hand over their rifles to their compatriots and whip out combat axes. Achilles and Twitch, both injured from the night’s fight already, try to strategize, and manage to knock both orks out of the fight, without getting knocked out themselves. Twitch stops Achilles from killing one, figuring the Comandante would appreciate restraint. He presents them both with berets featuring the group’s sigil, and whisks them away in 2 vans. They get a membership count and some facial images, which Shri forwards to Izidor, but the vans are jammed, and she loses them for a while before they pop up for a moment in a nearby Z-zone, due to Twitch’s satellite link. She tells them to blend in and see what they can learn, and report in when possible.

They watch training trids, and receive the relevant indoctrination. Achilles is really excited at first, but realizes that he doesn’t share the group’s anti-corp fervor. Twitch plays along, but tries not to get invested. The members seem to train constantly, and meditate when not training. They don’t discriminate amongst corp targets: labs, corp citizens, researchers, stocks/stores, anything at all seems to be a legit target. There seems to be only about a dozen members, though, as they say they lost some recently, and recruited these 2 to take their place, in preparation for an upcoming mission (which will come down the pipeline from a different cell to the Comandante).

They find out the target, and Twitch gets a message off the Shri as they load in the vans and head out. She warns Izidor, and asks him to make sure her team gets out ok. He agrees to try. Twitch manages to sneak off as the others in his van bust through the gate at the pier-side AZT facility, but Achilles’ van races directly in and he is unable to bail before it is hit by a missile and gatling fire from a HTR chopper. His half of the strike team is gunned down, and he is captured as the other half of the team stages a fighting retreat. Twitch and Shri link up, and debrief with Izidor, after which he gives them the info they sought. Twitch heads to NYC to link up with Munty for another job, having proven himself useful to Pia and the team.

All of the chatter on the matrix about him was also faked, which was apparent once the time/date stamps and other markers were closely examined. He also doesn’t work for AZT, as he was hinting, which makes sense as AZT hasn’t made any gains in the wake of the run, and are in fact being sued at the Corporate Court for their “involvement.” However, Evo Corporation has benefited significantly, securing contracts making them the second largest corp presence in the Sioux Nation after Ares Macrotechnology. It seems that Mr. Johnson was working for them instead. They also receive a pic of him (as he was wearing a disguise during their meet), and his real name: Theo Two-Hearts. He was apparently the heir apparent to the “old man” who ran WRC for a generation. After the old man’s recent death, the rest of the family forced Theo out, due to his mixed Native/Caucasian ancestry, preferring that a pure Sioux member take control. Theo seems to have lost it, and using resources and tricks learned under the old man’s tutelage, to have devised his scheme to ruin WRC, and secure himself a cushy spot in a different corp. Shri relays this to Pia and the team, and they begin scheming…

Meanwhile, Achilles wakes up after a day in a brightly lit interrogation room, trapped in a bolted-down chair with fused manacles. After a few moments, a very friendly man with an Aztlaner accent saunters in and seats himself. He cheerily breaks Achilles down through a series of question, statements, and revelations, and forces him to realize that he won’t be leaving here without providing some info. He’s also really friendly, which throws Achilles off. He gives up a SIN each of Shri’s, Munty’s, Caria’s, and Tenten’s (not knowing he is already dead), as well as all the details of the run against WRC. At the end, the man talks him into signing his statement (which perhaps AZT will try to use to escape charges at the CC?) before leaving the room. A short while later, 2 large humans enter, and defuse Achilles, before roughly escorting him down a winding series of passages, and tossing him out a brick door onto a rotting dock.

He wanders a bit to get a signal, and gets ahold of Shri, who seems suspicious, but agrees to meet him at the nearest Ork Underground entrance, and bring him in. They return to the safehouse, and he reveals his somewhat accidental (or at least non-voluntary) treachery. Shri, reminded too closely of her own past, walks out to clear her head (or perhaps muddy it further) and everyone else debates what to do…

Ro tries to play it cool, but Rayen menacingly says that they will see each other again, using Ro’s real name (which she somehow found out).

The team agrees.

They do some research, and find that Aleph is doing outreach at Camp Lincoln in the CZ. Doing some research, and calling Lothan for info, they find out that Chem and Ortega’s paranoia about Camp Lincoln is somewhat misplaced- although they may also be cannibals, they are primarily a community living in the park which knows how to make willing people ‘disappear’, for a price. They have some sort of connection to Spider, who hates insects, so they imagine there are some shamans about. The team reaches the camp, and following a web-like maze, emerge into a clearing where a tent and some benches have been set up. An Aleph barker calls out for all shattered souls to join them in their healing wisdom.

They make it through a propagandistic meeting, and pay upfront dues to move in as 1st level students at the Society’s campus. They hide their illicit gear in a smuggling compartment in the van and park it securely nearby, but are stripped of their possession and told they must work without magical assistance to appreciate fully the gifts they will receive. They spend a week opening up another housing block, as the Society appears to be attracting many new members, before they move up a level, and start receiving lectures on the history of the Society. They still work, but Ro and Toff manage to cover for Munty as she sneaks around and recons. She finds that the lecturers (and high level initiates) all live in an old admin building, with warded lower levels. She figures out what security devices they need to bypass to enter.

At the final lecture, some high level acolytes pull a man from the crowd, who they claim is an ex-insect shaman trying to infiltrate the order to get power back. Before the 2nd-tier students, they burn the man alive inside of a force sphere, so they are unable to hear his screams as the lecturer rants about maintaining the purity of Aleph. Munty manages to sweet talk him after the lecture long enough to copy his prints, and Toff uses clairaudience to overhear the vocal code. Munty manages to sneak into the office with these. Toff and Ro notice that a number of other students left in the wake of the burning, and think Munty’s absence should be dismissable as such. They are told they will be required to swear fealty the next day.

Munty hides out inside in a vent, waiting for a low-traffic time. Toff and Ro and awoken in the middle of the night by cloaked figures carrying torches and told the fealty ritual can’t wait. They are brought via levitation to the top of the admin building, while Munty begins sneaking into the basement inside. They partake in the ritual, which uses a small amount of blood and drains them of some karma. Toff sees that in the astral they all now have a thin bond to some distant metaplane, but he can’t tell which one. They then have a celebration/meet and greet with the acolytes who brought them there, as well as the Society’s current leader, Sierra LaGuardia. Toff and Ro decide to use the page to try to get more info before they get deeper in, and con LaGuardia, who seems eager for more ‘sacred books’- she apparently has 2 and seeks a 3rd, claiming they are relics of Atlantis.

She has the page, the runners, and 2 acolytes brought to her office, where her initial examination, and their explanation of where they found it (claiming they retrieved it from The Foul One’s lair) seem to pass muster. She then leads them down to the basement. Munty, meanwhile, has been exploring, and managed to sneak through the physical plant into a sub-basement using a vocal sample of LaGuardia that Ro sent along. Munty finds a series of 4 surveilled hallways wrapping around a seemingly perfectly smooth concrete cube that runs floor to ceiling. Unable to find a way in, she briefly despairs, before hearing the others descending the stairs and runs and hides.

They enter the cube after LaGaurdia shapes open a door, and Munty manages to sneak in right behind them as it closes, while Ro distracts. They proceed past an armed guard into a library, while Munty hangs back and tases the guard, very quietly. She slips in the library door, just as the others exit the far side, after LaGuardia returns one of the sacred tomes (used in the fealty ritual) to its proper place. Munty begins flipping through and photographing both The Book of Gaf and The Book of Tak, before finding the logs of the secret history of the order. She hears some distant explosions and rumblings, and takes cover.

Meanwhile, the rest of the team has entered a shadowy room with a large, shaded sphere occupying almost all the available space. Toff briefly assenses, and sees that this is likely a metaplanar gate of some sort, and realizes that 2 shadowy spirit forms seem to be the end destination of the astral threads that they all gained in the ritual. LaGuardia walks into the sphere, seemingly supported by nothing, and plays the page on a shadow altar. It lights into flame and disintegrates, and LaGaurdia calls out as the spirits seem to begin draining something of her, with everyone hearing a dry and crackled voice saying that “this is not a true revelation.” The acolytes seem briefly unsure what to do, and Toff manages to magic open the only exit as they attack Ro. With Munty’s help, they put them down, but hear more explosions nearer by.

They hide as best they can as a buffed-up LaGuardia emerges from the shadow sphere trailing it’s aura. Some cybered-up mercs, seemingly from the Society of the Phoenix Arisen based on their armor, enter from the opposite side, having breached the door, and open fire. The bullets seem to bounce off LaGuardia, a power the team has only seen on spirits before, with her quickly healing any damage she does take. She crushes one of the mercs in some kind of gravity sphere. The team sneaks out, but one of the mercs nearly guns down Ro before getting distracted by spirit magic. They manage to make good their escape amidst the chaos- it looks like Phoenix Arisen is taking revenge for the dead amongst their number at their disastrous holiday party in Seattle the year before.

They reach Sanctum again, and the ASPS manages to break their blood pact before it drains them much further. They are healed up and receive their pay, as well as passing the info along. Ro and Toff both also pass on the general info (but not the ritual specifics) to Renraku Computer Systems and the Dragon Church, respectively. The ASPS strongly requests they keep the specifics secret, as they are too dangerous to be out in the public- many burnouts are desperate enough to attempt just such a ritual to get their mojo back.

Ro was kept around, as the most stable build, and kind of a test if the theoretical practices could actually work. Her father was snatched up while they were boating together, which explains some things. She seems to be the only survivor.

Aemon, mourning his essence loss, joins a Black Star raid on the nearby Human Brigade/Humanis Nation turf. They slaughter some border guards, and then one the hit squad, posing as a guard, lures some families from their homes while the rest of the team guns them down. Aemon tries to injure the children in such a way that they will survive but not get shot further, usually trick-shooting them in the legs. He returns to the base, never having seen the face of any of the people he did that with. They seemed to want revenge for the Omega Dawn killings, which they blamed on the metaracists, as they happened near their turf. Aemon feels awful about what he did, but can’t admit it to anyone (especially Ortega). He confides that something bad happened to TY, who tries to get him to open up by sharing his own horrifying past. Chessick, sensing something is off with Aemon, also tries to draw him out, but to no avail.

After everyone has healed and re-equipped from the last run, TY hires them to help him track down a local Gilgamesh Initiative base that April Halfwoman gave him clues to. They arrange to park the van at Freaktown nearby, and proceed on foot to an area near the Truman Tower and Shattergraves. Although they’ve acclimated to the general CZ background count, this area has a bad feel about it. They surveil for 4 days, tightening their perimeter, until they ID the building they seek, based on a troll on a motorcycle seemingly doing supply runs. Chessick and TY disable the exterior security, and they make their way down through the ruined building to a secure vault door set into the floor of the basement. Chessick gets it open, and they descend some poorly-lit concrete stairs winding down a cylindrical shaft. The troll seems to have just ridden his bike down, an impressive feat.

They reach the bottom, and manage to open an earth-core security door, as the vault door irises shut above them. Toff feels very distraught, as they are now cut off from the astral plane, and he brought a spirit down- if ti dies here he doesn’t know what will happen.
